          if [ "$DRY_RUN" = "true" ]; then
            say "Dry run: would start CI on main with runner=github, then cancel the runs above."
            exit 0
          fi

          # A minute's grace for the runner's clock and GitHub's to disagree:
          # a recovery run stamped a second before this one's idea of now
          # would otherwise never be seen, and the watchdog would stop.
          started=$(date -u -d '-1 minute' +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
          gh workflow run ci.yml --repo "$REPO" --ref main -f runner=github

          # Wait to see the recovery run before cancelling anything. Cancelling
          # the only run that would publish, with nothing to replace it, is
          # the failure this workflow exists to prevent.
          seen=""
          for _ in $(seq 1 12); do
            sleep 5
            seen=$(gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/ci.yml/runs?event=workflow_dispatch&branch=main&per_page=10" \
              --jq "[.workflow_runs[] | select(.created_at >= \"$started\") | .id] | first // empty")
            [ -n "$seen" ] && break
          done
          if [ -z "$seen" ]; then
            echo "::error::Asked GitHub for a recovery run and none appeared within a minute, so nothing was cancelled. Check the Actions tab, and dispatch CI on main with runner=github by hand."
            exit 1
          fi
          say "Started recovery run $seen on GitHub's machines."

          for id in $blockers; do
            if gh api -X POST "repos/$REPO/actions/runs/$id/cancel" >/dev/null; then
              say "Cancelled run $id, which was holding the slot the recovery run needs."
            else
              echo "::warning::Could not cancel run $id; the recovery run will wait until it finishes."
            fi
          done

          echo "::notice::main's CI was stuck for ${waited}m; started recovery run $seen on GitHub's machines."

name: Website

# Publishes zoomies.sh from the docs that live in docs/, so the site cannot
# drift from the repository: the build is checked, then deployed to the site
# worker's static assets, which is where the domain is served from. install.sh
# and install.ps1 land in the site root the same way, so the script people curl
# (or irm) and the script a contributor edits are the same file. The worker's
# tests run here too: the copies it serves for Accept: text/markdown come out
# of this build.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "docs/**"
      - "overrides/**"
      - "hooks/**"
      - "site-worker/**"
      - "skills/**"
      - "mkdocs.yml"
      - "install.sh"
      - "install.ps1"
      - "connect-proxmox.sh"
      - ".github/workflows/docs.yml"
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, closed]
    paths:
      - "docs/**"
      - "overrides/**"
      - "hooks/**"
      - "site-worker/**"
      - "skills/**"
      - "mkdocs.yml"
      - "install.sh"
      - "install.ps1"
      - "connect-proxmox.sh"
      - ".github/workflows/docs.yml"
  # The header names the latest release, resolved when the site is built
  # (hooks/source.py). A release that did not rebuild the site would leave it
  # naming the one before until the daily build below caught up.
  release:
    types: [published]
  # A failed publish takes the whole site with it: pushes only build this
  # workflow when something under docs/ changed, so the last good deploy stays
  # up -- missing whatever the failed one carried -- until somebody happens to
  # edit the documentation again. The build is a couple of minutes and produces
  # the same site when nothing changed, so rebuild it daily: a runner having a
  # bad day then costs the site a day, not a fortnight.
  schedule:
    - cron: "29 4 * * *" # daily at 04:29 UTC
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: "Where to build. github is the escape hatch from a single vendor."
        type: choice
        default: blacksmith
        options: [blacksmith, github]

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  # One group per pull request, and one per ref for everything else. A pull
  # request's build is replaced by a newer push and dropped when the pull
  # request closes, as in ci.yml; no other run is ever cancelled. Deployments
  # only happen from main, so they queue in main's group.
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  refresh-release:
    name: Refresh the website from main
    # A release run belongs to its tag even if checkout selects main, so a
    # release asks for a new run whose ref really is main.
    # workflow_dispatch can be triggered by GITHUB_TOKEN.
    if: github.event.action != 'closed' && github.event_name == 'release'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10 # the longest successful run seen was under a minute
    permissions:
      actions: write
    steps:
      - name: Start the website workflow on main
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: gh workflow run docs.yml --repo "$REPO" --ref main

  build:
    name: Build
    # The main-branch run requested above owns both the build and deployment.
    if: github.event.action != 'closed' && github.event_name != 'release'
    env:
      # The IndexNow key. Not a secret: the protocol proves ownership by this
      # key being served as docs/<key>.txt at the site root, where anyone can
      # read it. See hooks/indexnow.py.
      INDEXNOW_KEY: d849cbc8f4ab6dbef799f56bd99d1475
    # The site is a mkdocs build with no vendor-specific step in it, so the
    # escape hatch here is one expression: publishing documentation must not be
    # impossible because a runner vendor is having a bad day.
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner == 'github' && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'blacksmith-4vcpu-ubuntu-2404' }}
    timeout-minutes: 15 # the longest successful run seen was 1 minute
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          # The sitemap stamps each URL with the date its page was last edited,
          # which is in the history. A shallow checkout has none, and every page
          # would claim to have changed on the day of the build.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"
          cache: pip
          cache-dependency-path: docs/requirements.txt

      - run: pip install --require-hashes -r docs/requirements.txt

      # --strict, so a link that points nowhere fails the build rather than
      # shipping. The docs cross-reference each other heavily.
      - name: Build
        env:
          # hooks/source.py asks the GitHub API for the latest release and the
          # repository's counts. Anonymous requests share one rate limit per
          # address, which a shared runner's address can already have spent.
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: mkdocs build --strict

      # The two files a crawler and an assistant look for first. Both are
      # generated, so a build that quietly stopped producing one would
      # otherwise ship a site nothing can index.
      - name: The sitemap, llms.txt, the Markdown copies and security.txt were produced
        run: |
          set -eu
          grep -q "https://zoomies.sh/quickstart/" site/sitemap.xml
          grep -q "https://zoomies.sh/faq/" site/llms.txt
          # Anchored to the file's own lines. A bare grep for a page's URL
          # also matches every link to it from another page, which for the
          # quickstart is dozens, so it passed with the page missing. A page
          # is either written out, under a "Canonical page:" line, or, over
          # _FULL_PAGE_LIMIT in hooks/seo.py, listed at the end with a link
          # to its own copy. The quickstart is the second today and either is
          # right; a short page that must be written out guards the first.
          grep -Eq '^(Canonical page: https://zoomies\.sh/quickstart/|- \[.*\]\(https://zoomies\.sh/quickstart/index\.md\))$' site/llms-full.txt
          grep -q '^Canonical page: https://zoomies.sh/what-are-self-hosted-runners/$' site/llms-full.txt
          grep -q "^# " site/quickstart/index.md
          grep -q "^# " site/index.md
          grep -q "^Contact: " site/.well-known/security.txt

      # The agent discovery documents name real endpoints and real artifacts,
      # so the build refuses to ship one that is empty JSON, names a digest no
      # skill copy answers to, or lost its auth.md heading.
      - name: The agent discovery documents are well formed
        run: |
          python3 - <<'EOF'
          import hashlib, json, os, re

          def load(path):
              with open("site/" + path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
                  return json.load(fh)

          auth = open("site/auth.md", encoding="utf-8").read()
          assert re.search(r"^# .*auth\.md", auth, re.MULTILINE), "auth.md has no auth.md heading"
          for marker in ("## Flows", "## Scopes", "## Registration", "/oauth/register", "oauth-protected-resource"):
              assert marker in auth, "auth.md lost " + marker

          card = load(".well-known/mcp/server-card.json")
          assert card["serverInfo"]["name"] == "zoomies"
          assert card["serverInfo"]["version"] and card["serverInfo"]["version"] != "0.0.0", "the card names no release"
          assert card["transport"]["endpoint"].startswith("https://")
          for key in ("tools", "resources", "prompts"):
              assert key in card["capabilities"], "the card does not name " + key
          assert card["authorization"]["scopesSupported"]

          index = load(".well-known/agent-skills/index.json")
          assert index["$schema"].endswith("/discovery/0.2.0/schema.json")
          assert index["skills"], "the index has no skills"
          for skill in index["skills"]:
              assert re.fullmatch(r"[a-z0-9-]+", skill["name"]), skill["name"]
              assert skill["type"] == "skill-md" and skill["description"] and skill["url"]
              folder = "site/.well-known/agent-skills/" + skill["name"] + "/"
              with open(folder + "SKILL.md", "rb") as fh:
                  body = fh.read()
              assert skill["digest"] == "sha256:" + hashlib.sha256(body).hexdigest(), skill["name"]
              # A skill reads its siblings by relative link, so each link has
              # to resolve beside the published SKILL.md. Published alone, the
              # zoomies skill sent an agent to a 404 for its command reference.
              for target in re.findall(r"\]\(([^)\s]+)\)", body.decode("utf-8")):
                  if "://" in target or target.startswith(("#", "mailto:")):
                      continue
                  linked = os.path.normpath(folder + target.split("#")[0])
                  assert linked.startswith(folder) and os.path.isfile(linked), skill["name"] + " links to " + target + ", which is not published beside its SKILL.md"

          for name in ("ai-catalog.json", "poppy.json", "api-catalog.json"):
              load(".well-known/" + name) if name != "api-catalog.json" else load(name)
          catalog = load(".well-known/ai-catalog.json")
          assert catalog["host"]["displayName"] and catalog["host"]["identifier"]
          for entry in catalog["entries"]:
              assert ("url" in entry) != ("data" in entry), entry["identifier"]
              assert 2 <= len(entry["representativeQueries"]) <= 5, entry["identifier"]
              # The type is what the url serves, and a page is text/html
              # whatever it is about: the REST entry once said application/yaml
              # of the API documentation's page.
              if entry.get("url", "").endswith("/"):
                  assert entry["type"] == "text/html", entry["identifier"] + " is a page, not " + entry["type"]
          # The host is named by a DID, and a DID that nothing resolves is a
          # claim nothing backs. did:web:zoomies.sh is read from
          # /.well-known/did.json.
          assert load(".well-known/did.json")["id"] == catalog["host"]["identifier"], "did.json does not describe the catalog's host"
          poppy = load(".well-known/poppy.json")
          assert poppy["organization"]["domain"] == "zoomies.sh"
          assert poppy["protocol_version"]
          agent = load(".well-known/agent-card.json")
          assert agent["name"] == "Zoomies" and agent["version"] and agent["version"] != "0.0.0", "the agent card names no release"
          assert agent["url"] == "https://demo.zoomies.sh/mcp", "the agent card does not name the demo's MCP endpoint"
          assert agent["capabilities"] is not None and agent["skills"], "the agent card has no capabilities or skills"
          for skill in agent["skills"]:
              assert skill["id"] and skill["name"] and skill["description"], skill["id"]
          assert agent["security"] and agent["securitySchemes"], "the agent card says nothing about signing in"
          for scheme in agent["securitySchemes"].values():
              assert scheme["type"] == "oauth2" and scheme["oauth2MetadataUrl"].endswith("/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server"), "the demo is an OAuth 2.0 server with RFC 8414 metadata and publishes no OpenID Connect discovery, so the card must not say otherwise"
          api_catalog = load("api-catalog.json")
          entry = api_catalog["linkset"][0]
          assert entry["status"][0]["href"] == "https://demo.zoomies.sh/readyz", entry
          print("discovery documents ok")
          EOF

      # The header's release, stars and forks are resolved at build time, and a
      # build that cannot reach the API still succeeds -- for a developer
      # offline, not for the site. A header that names no release is the thing
      # this exists to prevent, so it does not ship.
      - name: The header names the latest release
        run: grep -q "md-source__fact--version" site/index.html

      # The badge is linked from READMEs the migration wizard has edited, out
      # in other people's repositories, and nothing in the docs build looks at
      # it: no page links to it, so --strict would not notice it going missing.
      # A broken image on somebody's front page is ours to prevent.
      - name: The CI has the Zoomies badge is published at the site root
        run: |
          set -eu
          test -s site/badge.svg

      - name: Publish install.sh at the site root
        run: |
          set -eu
          # One source of truth. `curl -fsSL https://zoomies.sh/install.sh | sh`
          # gets exactly the file in this repository's root.
          cp install.sh site/install.sh
          # A courtesy alias, because people type both.
          cp install.sh site/install
          # The same for Windows: `irm https://zoomies.sh/install.ps1`.
          cp install.ps1 site/install.ps1
          # The provider wizard's short Proxmox command fetches this one.
          cp connect-proxmox.sh site/connect-proxmox.sh

      # The edge worker answers Accept: text/markdown with the copies the build
      # just wrote, on the Accept header GitHub Pages cannot read. Its rules
      # are tested against an in-memory origin, so a change to either side
      # alone is caught here rather than on the site.
      - name: The edge worker's negotiation is still right
        run: node --test site-worker/worker.test.mjs

      # IndexNow tells Bing and the other participating engines which pages
      # changed, rather than waiting for them to recrawl. The protocol trusts a
      # submission only if the key file is served at the site root, so a build
      # that stopped publishing it would have every submission ignored.
      - name: The IndexNow key file is published at the site root
        run: |
          set -eu
          test "$(cat "site/${INDEXNOW_KEY}.txt")" = "${INDEXNOW_KEY}"

      # Compared against the sitemap that is live now, before this build
      # replaces it: only new pages and pages whose last-edited date moved are
      # submitted. It never fails the build.
      - name: Work out which pages changed, for IndexNow
        id: indexnow
        run: python hooks/indexnow.py site/sitemap.xml https://zoomies.sh/sitemap.xml "${INDEXNOW_KEY}"

      - name: The published install.sh is byte-identical to the repository's
        run: cmp install.sh site/install.sh

      - name: The published install.ps1 is byte-identical to the repository's
        run: cmp install.ps1 site/install.ps1

      - name: It is still valid POSIX sh after publishing
        run: dash -n site/install.sh

      - name: The published connect-proxmox.sh is byte-identical and valid POSIX sh
        run: |
          set -eu
          cmp connect-proxmox.sh site/connect-proxmox.sh
          dash -n site/connect-proxmox.sh

      # The scripts people pipe into a shell are copied into site/ by a build
      # step, so a deploy of a plain `mkdocs build` (run by hand with wrangler)
      # ships a site whose install commands all answer 404. Nothing is uploaded
      # unless they are in the directory that becomes the assets.
      - name: The installer scripts are in the directory the edge will serve
        run: |
          set -eu
          for f in install.sh install install.ps1 connect-proxmox.sh; do
            test -s "site/$f" || { echo "::error::site/$f is missing, so the deploy would 404 the install commands"; exit 1; }
          done

      # The site is served by the edge worker from this build's static assets.
      # Deploying from the job that built and checked it keeps one artefact:
      # the upload is the publish.
      - name: Deploy the site to the edge
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        working-directory: site-worker
        env:
          CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN }}
          CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID: ${{ secrets.CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID }}
        run: npx --yes wrangler@4.151.1 deploy

      # What the build holds says nothing about what the edge answers, and a
      # deploy made from somewhere else can replace it between runs. The
      # published script is fetched the way a user's `curl -fsSL` fetches it.
      - name: The live site serves the installer scripts
        if: github.event_name != 'pull_request' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        run: |
          set -eu
          for f in install.sh install.ps1 connect-proxmox.sh; do
            ok=
            for attempt in 1 2 3 4 5 6; do
              if curl -fsSL "https://zoomies.sh/$f?check=$GITHUB_RUN_ID" | cmp -s - "site/$f"; then ok=1; break; fi
              sleep 10
            done
            test -n "$ok" || { echo "::error::https://zoomies.sh/$f is not serving the published file"; exit 1; }
          done

      # After the deploy, not before: an engine told about a page fetches it
      # straight away, and it has to find the new one. A failed submission is
      # reported and does not fail the deploy -- the site is up, and the
      # sitemap will get the pages found regardless.
      - name: Tell IndexNow which pages changed
        if: steps.indexnow.outputs.payload != ''
        env:
          PAYLOAD: ${{ steps.indexnow.outputs.payload }}
        run: |
          set -u
          status=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' -X POST \
            -H 'Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8' \
            --data "$PAYLOAD" https://api.indexnow.org/indexnow) || status=unreachable
          case "$status" in
            200|202) echo "IndexNow accepted the submission ($status)" ;;
            *) echo "::warning::IndexNow did not accept the submission ($status)" ;;
          esac

name: Fuzz

# The fuzz targets are the boundaries that read what a stranger wrote: the
# encryption in internal/cryptox and the workflow parser in
# internal/kennel/workflow. Only a change there, or to the toolchain they are
# built with, can find anything new. The weekly run keeps fuzzing main
# regardless.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "internal/cryptox/**"
      - "internal/kennel/workflow/**"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
      - ".github/workflows/fuzz.yml"
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, closed]
    paths:
      - "internal/cryptox/**"
      - "internal/kennel/workflow/**"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
      - ".github/workflows/fuzz.yml"
  schedule:
    - cron: "31 5 * * 2"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: "Where to fuzz. github is the recovery path."
        type: choice
        default: zoomies
        options: [zoomies, github]

permissions:
  contents: read

# A pull request's fuzzing is replaced by a newer push and dropped when the
# pull request is closed or merged, rather than left to spend a fleet slot on a
# result nobody will read. Main's runs and the weekly one, which fuzzes for
# longer, are never cancelled. ci.yml says why.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

jobs:
  fuzz:
    if: github.event.action != 'closed'
    # The Zoomies pool, except for a fork's pull request, whose code must not
    # run on the fleet, and a manual dispatch that asks for GitHub's runners.
    # ci.yml and govulncheck.yml choose the same way, and a test in internal/docs
    # holds all three to it.
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    timeout-minutes: 30
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - { target: FuzzParseKey, package: ./internal/cryptox }
          - { target: FuzzSealOpen, package: ./internal/cryptox }
          # The workflow parser reads what a pull request author wrote. Every
          # fuzz target in the repository has a row here: a test in
          # internal/docs fails on one that does not.
          - { target: FuzzInspect, package: ./internal/kennel/workflow }
          - { target: FuzzCheckoutDepthEditPreservesTheDocument, package: ./internal/kennel/workflow }
          - { target: FuzzDependencyInventoriesPreserveTheirRetainedInvariants, package: ./internal/kennel/workflow }
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-go
      - name: Fuzz the boundary
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
          PACKAGE: ${{ matrix.package }}
          DURATION: ${{ github.event_name == 'schedule' && '5m' || '30s' }}
        run: go test "$PACKAGE" -run '^$' -fuzz "^${TARGET}$" -fuzztime "$DURATION" -parallel 2
      - name: Preserve failing inputs
        if: failure()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: fuzz-corpus-${{ matrix.target }}
          path: ${{ matrix.package }}/testdata/fuzz/
          if-no-files-found: ignore

name: govulncheck

# A module that was clean when it was merged can be found vulnerable later,
# and nothing in CI would run again to say so. This scans the Go modules on
# every change to Go or its modules and once a week against main, and it lives outside ci.yml so
# the weekly run is this one job rather than the whole pipeline. govulncheck
# reports a vulnerability only when the code can reach it, which is what makes
# it quiet enough to block a pull request on.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - "**.go"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
      - ".github/workflows/govulncheck.yml"
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize, reopened, closed]
    paths:
      - "**.go"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
      - ".github/workflows/govulncheck.yml"
  schedule:
    - cron: "37 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: "Where to scan. github is the recovery path."
        type: choice
        default: zoomies
        options: [zoomies, github]

permissions:
  contents: read

# A pull request's scan is replaced by a newer push and dropped when the pull
# request is closed or merged. Main's runs and the weekly one are never
# cancelled: a scan that was cut short reports nothing. ci.yml says why.
concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

# The Go version is in .github/actions/setup-go, which every job uses.

jobs:
  govulncheck:
    name: govulncheck
    if: github.event.action != 'closed'
    # Fork code never reaches the self-hosted fleet. A manual dispatch can use
    # GitHub-hosted capacity if the Zoomies pool is unavailable.
    runs-on: ${{ ((github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.runner == 'github') || (github.event_name == 'pull_request' && github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork)) && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    timeout-minutes: 20 # the longest successful run seen was 3 minutes
    # Bound the scanner and compiler on small runner containers. A killed
    # scanner has no result; keep the full reachable-code scan enabled.
    env:
      GOMAXPROCS: "2"
      GOMEMLIMIT: "768MiB"
      GOFLAGS: "-p=1"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-go

      # go:embed needs the directory to exist even when the UI is not built.
      - name: Stub the embedded UI
        timeout-minutes: 1
        run: make ui-stub

      # The scanner is a dependency too, so it is pinned like the actions are.
      - run: go run golang.org/x/vuln/cmd/govulncheck@v1.7.0 ./...

name: Image health

# A tag that resolves is not a tag that pulls. A multi-platform tag is an
# index, and if one of the manifests it lists is deleted the registry still
# answers for the tag while `docker pull` fails with "manifest unknown" -- which
# is how v1.3.2 and :latest broke without anything going red. This walks the
# tags people actually pull, every day and after every release, and fails
# loudly when a child manifest is missing.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 6 * * *" # daily at 06:17 UTC
  release:
    types: [published]
  # Straight after the nightly package cleanup, so a deletion that breaks a
  # tag is caught the same night rather than at 06:17.
  workflow_run:
    workflows: [Cleanup Old Container Images]
    types: [completed]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions: {}

jobs:
  check:
    permissions:
      contents: read
    name: Check ${{ matrix.package }}
    # GitHub-hosted on purpose: whether the images pull must not depend on the
    # fleet those images run.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 90 # the longest successful run seen was 30 minutes
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        package:
          - zoomies
          - zoomies-agent
          - zoomies-runner
          - zoomies-runner-docker
          - zoomies-runner-full
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Check latest, dev and the release in question
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          PACKAGE: ${{ matrix.package }}
          # The release that triggered this run, prerelease or not. Looking up
          # "the newest full release" instead would check an older tag and
          # pass while the new one is broken.
          RELEASE_TAG: ${{ github.event.release.tag_name }}
        run: |
          set -eu
          if [ "$GITHUB_EVENT_NAME" = "release" ]; then
            # The image jobs push after the release is published; give them time.
            sleep 1800
            tag=$RELEASE_TAG
          else
            tag=$(gh release list --repo "$GITHUB_REPOSITORY" --exclude-drafts --exclude-pre-releases \
              --limit 1 --json tagName --jq '.[0].tagName')
          fi
          if ! .github/scripts/ghcr-check-tags.sh "$PACKAGE" latest dev "$tag"; then
            echo "::error::ghcr.io/eyupio/$PACKAGE has a tag that no longer pulls. See docs/development/image-recovery.md."
            exit 1
          fi

---
name: OpenCode
on:
  issue_comment:
    types: [created]
  pull_request_review_comment:
    types: [created]
# Nothing by default: the one job below asks for what it needs, in its own block,
# so the write grant sits beside the condition that guards it.
permissions: {}
jobs:
  opencode:
    # One agent run per issue or pull request at a time. A second `/oc` while the
    # first is working would race it to push to the same branch, so it waits
    # rather than cancelling: cancelling would discard work somebody asked for.
    # The group is on the job, not the workflow, on purpose. Every comment starts
    # a run, and a workflow-level group would let an ordinary comment, whose job
    # is skipped, replace a queued `/oc` that is waiting its turn.
    concurrency:
      group: opencode-${{ github.event.issue.number || github.event.pull_request.number }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    # The repository secret OPENCODE_API_KEY pays for the model; it is set under
    # Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions. id-token is held for the action,
    # and whether it needs it has not been established.
    permissions:
      contents: write
      issues: write
      pull-requests: write
      id-token: write
    # Anyone who can comment can write '/oc', and this job holds write tokens
    # and a paid API key, so the trigger alone is not enough: only someone the
    # repository already trusts may start it. A stranger's comment is ignored.
    if: >-
      (contains(github.event.comment.body, '/oc') || contains(github.event.comment.body, '/opencode'))
      && contains(fromJSON('["OWNER", "MEMBER", "COLLABORATOR"]'), github.event.comment.author_association)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60 # the longest successful run seen was 32 minutes
    steps:
      - name: Checkout repository
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1  # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
      - name: Run OpenCode
        uses: dceoy/opencode-action@4ac2dcfedc831e91174efd2f0fec2aa2f4bbaa79  # v0.8.0
        env:
          OPENCODE_API_KEY: ${{ secrets.OPENCODE_API_KEY }}
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        with:
          model: opencode-go/kimi-k3

name: Refresh the runner images' bases

# Every runner image is built FROM a base pinned by digest, so that an image built
# next year is built on the base it was tested on. A pin that nothing moves ages,
# and these were not seen by anything: they reach deploy/Dockerfile.runner as
# build arguments, written from the table in internal/naming/images.go, which
# Dependabot cannot read. Five of the seven were behind their registries, every
# Ubuntu and Debian base among them.
#
# This asks each registry what each tag points at today and opens a pull request
# when any moved. It is reviewed like any other change to what the images are
# made of, and CI builds every variant on it. `make runner-bases` does the same
# by hand.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "47 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: "Where to run. github is the recovery path."
        type: choice
        default: zoomies
        options: [zoomies, github]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  refresh:
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner == 'github' && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    timeout-minutes: 30 # a few minutes: seven manifest requests and a short compile
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-go

      # Moves the digests in internal/naming/images.go and rewrites what the table
      # feeds: the Makefile's variant rows, both workflows' build matrices and the
      # table in docs/naming.md. It changes nothing when no base has moved.
      #
      # pipefail, because the default shell has none: a registry that answered 429
      # made the generator fail, tee reported success, and the step went green
      # with no pull request and nothing to say the pins had not been looked at.
      - name: Move the pins
        run: |
          set -eu -o pipefail
          make runner-bases | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/moved.txt"

      - name: Describe what moved
        run: |
          set -eu
          {
            echo "Each runner image is built from a base pinned by digest. These bases have"
            echo "a newer image behind the same tag than the one pinned:"
            echo
            echo '```'
            grep -e '->' "$RUNNER_TEMP/moved.txt" || true
            echo '```'
            echo
            echo "Generated by \`make runner-bases\`: the digests in internal/naming/images.go,"
            echo "and what is derived from them. CI builds every variant on this pull request."
          } > "$RUNNER_TEMP/body.md"

      - name: Open a pull request
        uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@5f6978faf089d4d20b00c7766989d076bb2fc7f1 # v8.1.1
        with:
          branch: chore/runner-bases
          title: "Refresh the runner images' base images"
          body-path: ${{ runner.temp }}/body.md
          commit-message: "Refresh the runner images' base images"

name: Check actions/runner version

# The runner image has to track the actions/runner release, because GitHub
# deprecates old runner versions and a stale image eventually stops working.
# This opens a pull request when a newer one appears.

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 6 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: "Where to run. github is the recovery path."
        type: choice
        default: zoomies
        options: [zoomies, github]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner == 'github' && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    timeout-minutes: 15 # the longest successful run seen was 2 minutes
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - id: latest
        name: Find the latest release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          latest=$(gh api repos/actions/runner/releases/latest --jq .tag_name | sed 's/^v//')
          current=$(grep -oP 'ARG RUNNER_VERSION=\K[0-9.]+' deploy/Dockerfile.runner)
          echo "latest=$latest"   >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "current=$current" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Current $current, latest $latest" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-go
        if: steps.latest.outputs.latest != steps.latest.outputs.current

      # Three places pin the release and one table holds its digests, and the
      # process backend refuses to install a version whose digests it lacks --
      # so the bump is only a bump when all four move together. The runner
      # image checks its download against the same digests, read back out of
      # the regenerated table so the two can never disagree.
      - name: Bump
        if: steps.latest.outputs.latest != steps.latest.outputs.current
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          v="${{ steps.latest.outputs.latest }}"
          sed -i "s/ARG RUNNER_VERSION=.*/ARG RUNNER_VERSION=$v/" deploy/Dockerfile.runner
          sed -i "s/^RUNNER_VERSION ?= .*/RUNNER_VERSION ?= $v/" Makefile
          sed -i "s/^const DefaultRunnerVersion = \".*\"/const DefaultRunnerVersion = \"$v\"/" internal/backend/process.go
          go run internal/backend/gen_runner_digests.go "$v"
          x64=$(grep -oP "actions-runner-linux-x64-$v.tar.gz\":\s*\"\K[0-9a-f]{64}" internal/backend/runner_digests.go)
          arm64=$(grep -oP "actions-runner-linux-arm64-$v.tar.gz\":\s*\"\K[0-9a-f]{64}" internal/backend/runner_digests.go)
          test -n "$x64" && test -n "$arm64"
          sed -i "s/^ARG RUNNER_SHA256_X64=.*/ARG RUNNER_SHA256_X64=$x64/" deploy/Dockerfile.runner
          sed -i "s/^ARG RUNNER_SHA256_ARM64=.*/ARG RUNNER_SHA256_ARM64=$arm64/" deploy/Dockerfile.runner

      - name: Open a pull request
        if: steps.latest.outputs.latest != steps.latest.outputs.current
        uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@5f6978faf089d4d20b00c7766989d076bb2fc7f1 # v8.1.1
        with:
          branch: chore/runner-${{ steps.latest.outputs.latest }}
          title: "Update the runner image to actions/runner ${{ steps.latest.outputs.latest }}"
          body: |
            actions/runner ${{ steps.latest.outputs.latest }} is out; the image
            currently pins ${{ steps.latest.outputs.current }}.

            Release notes:
            https://github.com/actions/runner/releases/tag/v${{ steps.latest.outputs.latest }}
          commit-message: "Update the runner image to actions/runner ${{ steps.latest.outputs.latest }}"

name: OpenSSF Scorecard

# Scorecard grades the workflows, the pinned dependencies, the images' base
# pins and the security policy; a push that changes none of them cannot move
# the grade. The weekly run re-reads the repository settings, which no push
# changes.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - ".github/**"
      - "deploy/**"
      # The docs site's lockfile and the AI context's are manifests the
      # Vulnerabilities check reads, and a fix for an advisory lands in one of
      # them. Without them here such a fix waits for Saturday's run to be seen.
      - "docs/requirements.txt"
      - "internal/aicontext/templates/package-lock.json"
      - "go.mod"
      - "go.sum"
      - "web/package.json"
      - "web/package-lock.json"
      - "SECURITY.md"
      # The Vulnerabilities check reads the ignore list that sits beside each
      # manifest it scans, so a change to any of them moves the check.
      - "osv-scanner.toml"
      - "**/osv-scanner.toml"
  schedule:
    # Re-evaluate repository and supply-chain posture every week.
    - cron: "23 7 * * 6"
  workflow_dispatch:

# Scorecard's publishing service requires read-only workflow defaults. The
# analysis job receives only the two write permissions needed for OIDC-backed
# result publication and GitHub code-scanning upload.
permissions: read-all

jobs:
  analysis:
    name: Scorecard analysis
    # The one job that cannot run on the fleet. Scorecard's publishing service
    # verifies the workflow that produced a result before it accepts one, and
    # it accepts results only from GitHub's own Ubuntu runners
    # (https://github.com/ossf/scorecard-action#workflow-restrictions). On
    # zoomies-linux-x64 the publish was refused with "invalid runner label",
    # no SARIF was written, and the upload below failed on every push to main.
    # Publishing is deliberately independent of the fleet being assessed
    # anyway: a score of the fleet's own supply chain should not depend on
    # the fleet being up.
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15 # the longest successful run seen was 1 minute
    permissions:
      security-events: write
      id-token: write

    steps:
      - name: Checkout code
        uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - name: Run analysis
        uses: ossf/scorecard-action@fa7117db83c52d787ae5a89f350999701505d78e # v2.5.0
        with:
          results_file: results.sarif
          results_format: sarif
          publish_results: true

      - name: Upload SARIF artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@cf430e030ddbb5b0abf93d22962f4752f3646cd9 # v7.0.2
        with:
          name: openssf-scorecard-sarif
          path: results.sarif
          retention-days: 5

      - name: Upload results to code scanning
        uses: github/codeql-action/upload-sarif@6f2ac81f5cd81fe351a197ba0b00d91d03cd2aee # v4.39.0
        with:
          sarif_file: results.sarif

name: Check the runner-full toolchains
# deploy/toolcache.lock pins every toolchain the runner-full image carries to
# one release and its digest. Python, Node.js, Go, Java and .NET all ship
# security fixes as patch releases, and an image that never moved would carry
# the day-one patch of each for ever. This reruns the generator every week
# and opens a pull request when any line has moved; the pull request's CI
# builds the image from it, which is what proves the new archives install.
on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "41 6 * * 2"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      runner:
        description: "Where to run. github is the recovery path."
        type: choice
        default: zoomies
        options: [zoomies, github]

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  check:
    permissions:
      contents: write
      pull-requests: write
    runs-on: ${{ inputs.runner == 'github' && 'ubuntu-latest' || 'zoomies-linux-x64' }}
    timeout-minutes: 15 # the longest successful run seen was 3 minutes
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup-go

      # A row whose archive is unchanged keeps the digest the lock already
      # holds, so a quiet week downloads nothing but the publishers' indexes,
      # and a Python patch downloads the six archives it moved.
      - name: Regenerate the lock
        run: go run deploy/gen_toolcache_lock.go

      - id: diff
        name: See what moved
        run: |
          set -eu
          if git diff --quiet -- deploy/toolcache.lock; then
            echo "changed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            echo "Every toolchain is on its newest release." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "changed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          {
            echo "summary<<EOF"
            # tool and version of every row that is new, one per line, once.
            git diff -U0 -- deploy/toolcache.lock | sed -n 's/^+\([a-z]*\) \([^ ]*\) .*/- \1 \2/p' | sort -u
            echo "EOF"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Open a pull request
        if: steps.diff.outputs.changed == 'true'
        uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@5f6978faf089d4d20b00c7766989d076bb2fc7f1 # v8.1.1
        with:
          branch: chore/toolcache
          title: "Move the runner-full toolchains to their newest releases"
          body: |
            `go run deploy/gen_toolcache_lock.go` moved these rows of
            `deploy/toolcache.lock`:

            ${{ steps.diff.outputs.summary }}

            The image build in this pull request's CI installs each archive
            against its digest and checks every toolchain answers.
          commit-message: "Move the runner-full toolchains to their newest releases"

# Managed by Zoomies AI Context; template 1. Review upgrades through a PR.
name: Zoomies AI Context
on:
  push:
    branches: ["main"]
  workflow_dispatch:
permissions:
  contents: read
concurrency:
  group: zoomies-ai-context
  cancel-in-progress: true
jobs:
  generate:
    if: "${{ github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' \u0026\u0026 (github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch') }}"
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 15
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          ref: ${{ github.sha }}
          path: source
          persist-credentials: false
          submodules: false
          lfs: false
      - uses: actions/setup-node@820762786026740c76f36085b0efc47a31fe5020 # v7.0.0
        with:
          node-version: '24'
          package-manager-cache: false
      - name: Install pinned generator without repository scripts
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -eu
          mkdir -p "$RUNNER_TEMP/zoomies-tools"
          cp source/.github/zoomies-ai-context/package.json "$RUNNER_TEMP/zoomies-tools/package.json"
          cp source/.github/zoomies-ai-context/package-lock.json "$RUNNER_TEMP/zoomies-tools/package-lock.json"
          npm ci --prefix "$RUNNER_TEMP/zoomies-tools" --ignore-scripts --no-audit --no-fund > /dev/null 2>&1
      - name: Generate bounded source context
        env:
          SOURCE_DIR: ${{ github.workspace }}/source
          OUTPUT_DIR: ${{ runner.temp }}/zoomies-context
          REPOMIX_CLI: ${{ runner.temp }}/zoomies-tools/node_modules/.bin/repomix
          SOURCE_COMMIT: ${{ github.sha }}
          EXPECTED_CONFIG: "{\"manager\":\"zoomies-ai-context\",\"template_version\":1,\"source_branch\":\"main\",\"destination\":\"both\",\"exclude\":[\"**/.env*\",\"**/node_modules/**\",\"**/.git/**\",\"**/dist/**\",\"**/vendor/**\",\"**/*.pem\",\"**/*.key\",\"**/*.db\",\".zoomies/**\"],\"keep_snapshots\":3,\"setup_generation\":4}"
          REPOSITORY_IDENTITY: "{\"github_host\":\"github.com\",\"installation_id\":\"ins_7xad5wpfjwbo6\",\"repository_id\":1357002726}"
          CONFIG_HASH: "45b0cae094227a89e12578e8e4559dbd2ec9bcdb848c02a3af62b583cff6f862"
        shell: python
        run: |
          # Managed by Zoomies AI Context. Repository text is data, never executable setup.
          import codecs
          import datetime
          import fnmatch
          import hashlib
          import json
          import os
          from pathlib import Path
          import re
          import subprocess
          import tempfile

          MAX_FILE = 1 << 20
          MAX_SOURCE = 24 << 20
          MAX_SNAPSHOT = 32 << 20
          MAX_FILES = 5000
          MAX_OMITTED = MAX_FILES
          OMIT_TOO_LARGE = 'too_large'
          OMIT_OVER_BUDGET = 'over_budget'
          OMIT_FLAGGED = 'flagged'


          class GenerationRefusal(ValueError):
              pass


          class OversizedText(GenerationRefusal):
              """A text file over MAX_FILE. Raised without the path so that source_blob
              stays free of repository text; build() names the file."""


          def command(*args, **kwargs):
              return subprocess.check_output(args, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL, **kwargs)


          def excluded(name, patterns):
              for pattern in patterns:
                  if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern):
                      return True
                  while pattern.startswith('**/'):
                      pattern = pattern[3:]
                      if fnmatch.fnmatchcase(name, pattern):
                          return True
              return False


          def safe_path(name):
              parts = name.split('/')
              return (name and len(name) <= 1024 and not name.startswith('/')
                      and not any(c in name for c in '\\\x00\r\n:')
                      and all(p not in ('', '.', '..') and p.lower() not in ('.git', 'node_modules', '.zoomies')
                              and not p.lower().startswith('.env') for p in parts)
                      and not name.lower().endswith(('.pem', '.key', '.p12', '.pfx', '.db', '.sqlite', '.sqlite3')))


          def source_blob(root, blob, size):
              # Bound reads even for enormous Git blobs. Detect binary data before
              # applying the text limit; brand images and PDFs are not source context.
              process = subprocess.Popen(['git', '-C', str(root), 'cat-file', 'blob', blob],
                                         stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
              try:
                  content = process.stdout.read(MAX_FILE + 1)
              finally:
                  process.stdout.close()
                  if size > MAX_FILE:
                      process.terminate()
                  status = process.wait()
              if size <= MAX_FILE and status != 0:
                  raise RuntimeError('Git blob could not be read')
              if b'\0' in content:
                  return None
              try:
                  # An oversized sample can end halfway through a UTF-8 character.
                  text = codecs.getincrementaldecoder('utf-8')().decode(content, final=size <= MAX_FILE)
              except UnicodeDecodeError:
                  return None
              if size > MAX_FILE:
                  raise OversizedText('A source file exceeds the context size limit; add an exclusion')
              return content, text


          def mib(size):
              return '%.1f MiB' % (size / (1 << 20))


          def human(size):
              if size < 1 << 10:
                  return '%d B' % size
              return '%.1f KiB' % (size / (1 << 10)) if size < 1 << 20 else mib(size)


          def within_budget(candidates):
              """Split {path: bytes} into what fits MAX_FILES and MAX_SOURCE and what does not.

              The largest files go first, ties by path, so the same commit always loses the
              same files and the most files survive: one big generated file should not cost
              a repository its hundreds of small ones."""
              kept = dict(candidates)
              total = sum(kept.values())
              dropped = []
              for name, size in sorted(candidates.items(), key=lambda item: (-item[1], item[0])):

## 2026-09-18 - Labels Are Normalized on the Way Out of the Store, Not Just on the Way In

**Learning:** `internal/scheduler`'s `Matches`/`Score`/`Eligible` each call `store.NormalizeLabels` on both the pool's and the job's `Labels` before comparing them, and `bestPool` calls all three per (job, pool) pair in `assign`'s loop over every queued job -- run on every reconcile tick. But `store.Pool.Labels` and `store.Job.Labels` are already normalized once when the store loads them (`queries_fleet.go:274,346`, `queries_events.go:68,146`), so the scheduler's hot path was re-deriving a value (dedupe map + `slices.Sort`) that was already correct on essentially every call. This wasn't visible as a classic N+1 or a loop-local allocation -- it looked like ordinary, already-pure label comparison code -- because the redundancy was between the *loader* and a *far-away caller*, not within one function.
**Action:** Before adding caching or restructuring a hot-path comparison function, check whether its input already satisfies the invariant the function establishes (sorted/deduped/normalized) by the time it's typically called -- grep the type's field for where it's assigned, not just where the "normalizing" function is called. When the invariant usually already holds, add an allocation-free `isXxx` fast-path check (no map, no sort) that returns the input unchanged, and fall back to the real work otherwise; this keeps the function correct for genuinely unnormalized input while eliminating the allocation and O(n log n) sort for the common case. Measured on `NormalizeLabels` with a 4-label already-normalized slice: 221.4 ns/op, 64 B/op, 1 alloc/op -> 61.71 ns/op, 0 B/op, 0 allocs/op (~3.6x, allocations eliminated).

## 2026-09-23 - `.jules/` and `.Jules/` both exist at repo root (case-collision risk)

**Finding:** The repo root carries two case-variant directories: `.jules/`
(`bolt.md`, `inspector.md`) and `.Jules/` (`scribe.md`). Different filenames in
each, so nothing is duplicated, but a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS,
Windows by default) cannot check out both at once, which is the exact problem
sub12 (a sibling repo) hit and fixed by merging down to one `.jules/`.

**Learning:** Nothing here caused a build failure because this sandbox's
filesystem is case-sensitive, so the collision is invisible until someone
clones on macOS/Windows and gets a permanently dirty working tree (one
directory silently shadowing the other, or a checkout error depending on the
tool). A case-collision like this can sit unnoticed indefinitely in CI and
only surface for a subset of contributors.

**Prevention:** Merging or removing a top-level directory is a "restructuring
directories" action and needs an explicit ask/PR a human reviews, not
something Groundskeeper does unilaterally. Left untouched this run. Fold
`.Jules/scribe.md` into `.jules/` (or vice versa) in a dedicated, human-reviewed
change, the way sub12 already did.

**Resolved 2026-10-15:** `.Jules/scribe.md` and `.Jules/testsmith.md` were moved
into `.jules/` with `git mv`, and `.Jules/` no longer exists. Nothing in the
repository referred to the `.Jules` spelling (a search for it found only this
entry), so no path needed updating.

**Finding:** `web/probe-usage.mjs`, `web/probe2.mjs` and `web/shot.mjs` were

actually invokes it. Grepping for the filename across scripts, configs and

# Inspector journal

## 2026-09-18 - `go test -race ./...` can spuriously time out `internal/controller` in this sandbox
**Finding:** A full `go test -race -count=1 ./...` run failed with `internal/controller` hitting the
10-minute per-package timeout, dumping hundreds of goroutines mid-migration. It reproduced once more
at a longer explicit `-timeout`, which first looked like a real deadlock worth chasing.
**Learning:** `internal/controller`'s tests each open a fresh SQLite store and run the full migration
set (`newHarness`), and modernc.org/sqlite (pure-Go) under the race detector is dramatically slower at
that than the interpreter overhead alone suggests. The same package passed in ~51s without `-race`, and
a plain `go test -count=1 ./...` (no race) passed cleanly on two separate full runs in this sandbox,
including immediately after a change that could not plausibly affect `internal/controller`. This reads
as sandbox CPU/resource contention under race instrumentation, not a deadlock or a regression.
**Prevention:** Before treating a `-race` timeout in `internal/controller` (or any package that opens
many fresh migrated stores) as a real bug, rerun the same package without `-race` and rerun the full
suite without `-race`. Only chase it as a deadlock if it reproduces there too. Don't burn a session's
budget re-running `-race` at ever-longer timeouts on a single package before doing that cheaper check.

## 2026-09-27 - Second consecutive run with no unambiguous defect; where the budget went
**Finding:** A full pass -- `go test -count=1 ./...` (all packages green), frontend `npm run test:unit`
(200/200), `npm run lint` (prettier + eslint clean), `npm run check` (svelte-check, 0 errors/warnings) --
plus close manual reading of the areas most likely to hide a real bug (DataGrid's abort/retry/live-refresh
machinery, the scheduler's busy/stillRunning drain guards, the usage-cost rollup's rounding, the Proxmox
provider's VMID allocation and node placement, the Usage/DateRange preset-vs-custom range math, form
double-submit guards across every `async function submit/save`, and ConfirmDialog coverage on every
destructive button) turned up nothing that wasn't already correct or a documented deliberate choice. This
is the second consecutive Inspector run on this repo to end this way (see PR #320, which found only a
stale doc comment across an equally thorough sweep of scheduler/controller/store/migrate/gateway/UI).
**Learning:** This repo's own review discipline (the exhaustive "why" comments, the matching test for
almost every invariant named in a comment) means a defect that survives to `main` is genuinely rare, not
that there is nothing left to check. Skimming files top-to-bottom for "smells" mostly re-confirms already-
correct code and burns budget without raising the odds of a real find.
**Prevention:** On this repo, spend the audit budget on *recently merged* work first (`git log --stat`
since the last Inspector PR) rather than a fresh top-to-bottom sweep -- a defect is far more likely to be
in code that hasn't yet had a review pass than in the long-settled core. If a full sweep still finds
nothing unambiguous, stop and skip the PR rather than forcing a low-value fix (a copy tweak, a comment
change) to have something to show; the instructions explicitly allow ending with no PR, and a previous run
already did exactly that for the same reason.

# Scribe's Journal: Zoomies

Critical documentation-drift learnings only. Routine fixes are not logged here.

## 2026-09-08 - Doc-completeness test had a blind spot: it only scanned one of two source files
Learning: `docs/problem-codes.md` claims to be checked "in both directions" by `internal/docs/codes_test.go`, and CLAUDE.md repeats that claim ("`internal/docs` tests in both directions"). But the test's `controllerSource` constant pointed only at `internal/controller/problems.go`. Two real, currently-emitted codes, `pool.dangerous` and `pool.cache_shared`, live in `internal/controller/views.go` (`PoolWarnings` / `cacheSharingWarning`), a file the test never parsed. Both `TestEveryProblemCodeIsDocumented` and `TestTheReferenceDescribesNoCodeThatIsGone` passed anyway, so the doc's own safety net had never actually covered these two rows.
Impact: An operator seeing `pool.dangerous` or `pool.cache_shared` in the UI's problems drawer had no reference row to look up what it means or how to fix it, exactly the failure the test exists to prevent, and the exact claim ("checked against the source by a test") in `docs/problem-codes.md` itself was false for these two codes.
Action: Added both rows to `docs/problem-codes.md`, and widened the test's source list (`controllerSources = []string{controllerSource, viewsSource}`) so a Problem literal anywhere in `internal/controller/` is caught, not just in `problems.go`. When a repo advertises "a test checks this," verify the test's own file list actually covers every place the checked-for thing can originate; a coverage claim is itself a claim worth spot-checking, not just the docs it backs.

# Sentinel journal

Short notes on security findings and the fixes made for them. One entry per
pull request, newest first.

## 2026-10-08: MCP discovery responses no-store without an external URL

When `security.mcp_oauth` is on and `server.external_url` is empty, the OAuth
discovery documents served at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource[/mcp]`
and `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` fill their issuer and endpoint
addresses from each request's `Host` header. The responses carried
`Cache-Control: public, max-age=300`. A shared HTTP cache keyed on URL alone
could then hand one caller's Host-derived answer back to another, sending a
later client to a forged authorisation server.

The config validator refuses this combination at startup when the controller
binds publicly, but allows it on loopback where the operator may be running
behind a reverse proxy that forwards whatever Host the client sent.

Fix: switch those three responses to `Cache-Control: no-store` whenever
`server.external_url` is empty. The cacheable path is unchanged when it is
set, so the issuer and endpoints are then a fixed address and sharing the
cached answer is safe.

# Testsmith's Journal: Zoomies

Critical test-coverage learnings only. Routine test additions are not logged here.

## 2026-09-27 - A helper's one conditional branch went untested across three call sites at once
Learning: `internal/scheduler/resources.go`'s `fieldFactor(p, typed)` returns `2` only when a field is both typed (operator-set, not derived from the host) and the pool runs docker-in-docker, and it is shared by `RunnerCharge`, `MinimumReserve` and `ReducedSize`. Every existing reduced-runner test happened to exercise a case where the condition is false: an automatic (untyped) DinD pool, or a typed non-DinD pool. The one combination that actually returns `2` -- a fixed-size DinD pool's reduced runner -- was placed and its per-container grant was asserted (`TestAReducedDockerInDockerPairSplitsWhatIsLeft`), but nothing fed that grant back through `RunnerCharge`/`Reserved` to check the doubling recovers the original host-side charge.
Risk: This is precisely the bug class the file's own comments describe as having shipped twice already, in both directions (charging one share while giving each container a whole one, and the mirror of it) -- a silent host-accounting drift that only shows up later as create timeouts on a machine the fleet believes is idle, or as a fleet refusing to use machines it has room on. Three functions sharing one helper meant one broken conditional would corrupt scheduling, minimum-reservation and reduced-sizing math simultaneously, and none of it would fail a test.
Action: When a helper's return value depends on a boolean combination (here: typed AND DinD), check that every *combination*, not just every call site, is covered by a test that traces the value through to an externally observable effect -- not just an intermediate value like a placement's per-container grant. Added `TestAReducedDockerInDockerRunnerIsChargedTwiceItsRow`, which places a reduced pair and then asserts `RunnerCharge`/`Reserved` double the row's stored allocation back to the charge. Verified it fails when the doubling condition is forced off.

# Agent guidance

Shared guidance for coding agents working in this repository.

## What this is

Zoomies is a self-hosted GitHub Actions runner fleet controller: one Go binary
that watches for queued jobs, starts an ephemeral runner container per job, and
destroys it when the job finishes. SQLite for state, a Svelte 5 UI embedded with
`go:embed`, no Kubernetes and no database server.

`cmd/zoomies` is the only binary. It is the controller (`zoomies controller`),
the agent (`zoomies agent`), the installer (`zoomies init`) and the CLI, chosen
by subcommand. On a single VM the controller runs an agent inside itself, so the
whole system is one process and one SQLite file.

Read [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) before changing anything
structural; it explains the shape and the reasons for it.

## Commands

```sh
make build-nogui   # build without rebuilding the UI (the fast inner loop)
make build         # build the UI and embed it (needs npm)
make test          # go test -race -count=1 ./...
make bench         # the benchmarks, six runs each; compare two runs with benchstat (BENCH, BENCH_PKGS, BENCH_COUNT narrow it)
make lint          # go vet, gofmt check, staticcheck if present, UI lint
make fmt           # gofmt + prettier
make dev           # controller with auth off, on :8080, for UI work
make ui-dev        # Vite dev server proxying /api to that controller
make test-unit     # the UI's unit tests: no browser, a few seconds
make test-ui       # Playwright against a real built binary
make openapi       # regenerate both copies of api/openapi.yaml: the embedded Go source and the UI's TypeScript client
make screenshots   # recapture docs/screenshots from the real UI, both themes (needs Pillow)
```

`go build ./...` fails on a clean checkout: `internal/api` embeds
`internal/api/webdist`, which is a build product. Run `make build-nogui` once,
it writes a placeholder, before any plain Go command (`go build`, `go vet`,
`go test`) that compiles that package. The `make` targets that run Go (`test`,
`test-short`, `bench`, `cover`, `lint`, `generate`) write the placeholder
themselves, and never over a real UI build. CI does the same thing as its first
step.

Go 1.27.1 or later (`go.mod` sets the floor; CI builds with 1.27.2), Node 22 or
later. Node is a build-time dependency only; the shipped binary is
self-contained and static (`CGO_ENABLED=0`, pure-Go SQLite).

Run a single test with `go test -run TestName ./internal/pkg/`. `make test-e2e`
needs real GitHub credentials and skips itself without them.

A change made for speed is held to a number: run `make bench` before and after
(on an otherwise idle machine, once per package, `tee`d to files) and put the
`benchstat` comparison in the commit message. `CONTRIBUTING.md` has the
commands. A benchmark checks that its scenario is the one its name describes
before it times anything; keep that when adding one.

## Package boundaries

These are load-bearing. Code that crosses them is the main thing to catch in
review.

| Package | Rule |
| --- | --- |
| `internal/store` | The **only** place SQL is written. Domain types, embedded migrations, every query. No other package imports `database/sql`. |
| `internal/scheduler` | **Pure.** `Decide` takes a snapshot and returns a `Plan`. No clock reads, no database, no network; that is what makes scaling behaviour testable, and it is where every decision's operator-facing *reason string* comes from. |
| `internal/updates` | **Pure.** `Choose` takes a list of releases, the mode, the soak and the instant, and picks the release the mode would take and says why. It imports the standard library and `internal/version` and reads no clock; `purity_test.go` enforces both. `Decide`, the planner for automatic updates, has joined it: it takes a snapshot and returns the actions and the sentence the status shows, under the same rules. |
| `internal/updates/channel` | The impure half of `internal/updates`: finds the update folder, writes a request into it and reads what the helper left. It is the only place the service touches that folder, and it never creates it (the installer does, with the service account's ownership). |
| `internal/api` | Transport only. A handler reads a request, asks the controller / auth / store, and renders the shape `api/openapi.yaml` promises. It has no opinions about the fleet. The resource views themselves (`HostView`, `PoolView`, …) are `internal/controller/views.go` types the handlers alias, because the event stream renders the same JSON and is fed from the controller. |
| `internal/provider` | The infrastructure-provider contract, a fake that obeys it, and `RunContractTests`, the conformance suite every provider passes. It may import `internal/store`'s domain types and `config.Finding` and **nothing else**; two tests enforce that, and that it names nothing provider-specific. Renting a machine is not placing a runner: this is separate from `internal/backend` on purpose. |
| `internal/provider/proxmox` | The first provider. The Proxmox VE API is hand-rolled `net/http` for the same reason the Docker one is. |
| `internal/controller` | Wiring: the reconcile loop, the machine loop, webhook ingest, the agent task queue, the log relay, and every payload the event stream carries (`views.go`, `derived.go`). The machine loop is **not** part of `Reconcile`: a clone takes minutes and `reconcileMu` is held for a whole scheduling pass. |
| `internal/config` | `zoomies.yaml` + `ZOOMIES_*` overrides, and the validator. |
| `internal/github` | App auth, JIT configs, webhook validation, the fallback poller, and `fake.go`, a fake GitHub used by tests. |
| `internal/backend` | Docker, Podman, bare process. The Docker API is hand-rolled `net/http` against the Engine API on purpose (see below). |
| `internal/agent` | The runner-executing half and its outbound transport. |
| `internal/mcp` | The MCP tools and both transports (stdio for `zoomies mcp`, Streamable HTTP for `/mcp`). A tool calls the REST API through the `mcp.API` interface and nothing else (no store, no controller), so it can never do what the caller's token could not. |

The rules that can be stated as an import are held by a test, not by review
alone: `internal/scheduler`, `internal/updates` and `internal/provider` each have
a purity or boundary test, `internal/mcp` may import only what its test lists,
and a test in `internal/store` fails if any other package's shipped code imports
`database/sql` or the SQLite driver. A test that fails on one of these names the
rule; when the import is a pure helper that belongs, add it to that test's
allowlist with a reason rather than loosening the rule.

Other invariants worth knowing before you edit:

* **The controller never dials an agent.** Agents connect outbound only (long-poll
  for tasks, POST results), so a host behind NAT needs no inbound rule. That is
  why log streaming is inverted: the controller queues a `stream_logs` task and
  the agent opens a chunked POST that gets relayed to the browser's SSE stream.
* **Webhook deliveries are at-least-once and can arrive out of order.** The jobs
  upsert refuses to move a job backwards through its lifecycle. Keep it that way.
* **Every `*.updated` event is the resource's `GET` shape.** The UI drops a frame
  straight into its cache, so a `host.updated` carrying a bare store row (no
  `healthy`, no `free`) repaints the host wrong. Publish through the
  controller's `publish*`/`Publish*` helpers, which render the view; never put a
  store row on the bus. `stats`, `problems.updated` and each host's view are
  computed after every pass and sent only when they change, so a new kind of
  problem (or a host whose slots or heartbeat moved with no row written)
  needs no publish call of its own.
Read the scoped guidance when working in these directories:

* [`internal/store/AGENTS.md`](internal/store/AGENTS.md): one writer, the runner state machine, sentinel errors, IDs.
* [`internal/config/AGENTS.md`](internal/config/AGENTS.md): configuration: settings live in the database.
* [`web/AGENTS.md`](web/AGENTS.md): the UI: tokens, status colours, no new libraries.
* [`internal/hosttune/AGENTS.md`](internal/hosttune/AGENTS.md): host health and tuning: consent, never tune from an upgrade, never restart Docker under work.
* [`.github/AGENTS.md`](.github/AGENTS.md): "Things CI will fail you on": the files CI diffs against their sources.

## Dependencies

Every dependency carries a one-line justification in
[docs/dependencies.md](docs/dependencies.md), and that is enforced by review.
Before adding one: could the standard library or fifty lines of our own do it?
Is it maintained? What does it pull in transitively? What does it cost against
the shell budget if it ships to the browser? Then add the row, in the same
voice, *why*, not *what*.

Some omissions are deliberate and documented there, notably
`github.com/docker/docker` (the hand-rolled Engine API client in
`internal/backend/dockerapi.go` is a few hundred lines and gets Podman almost
free, because `podman.sock` speaks the same protocol).

## Testing

Table-driven and standard-library `testing` throughout; no assertion framework.
Tests use `:memory:` SQLite stores, injected clocks (`store.Options.Now`), and
the fake GitHub in `internal/github/fake.go` rather than network calls. Helper
constructors take `t` and call `t.Helper()` / `t.Cleanup`. Coverage is broad
(roughly one test file for every source file) so a new behaviour is expected to
arrive with one.

Test names are sentences about the behaviour, not the method
(`TestOpenCreatesTheDatabaseDirectory`), and a test often carries a comment
explaining *why the behaviour matters*, not what the code does.

## Voice

The prose in this repository (comments, docs, error messages, commit messages)
has a consistent voice, and matching it is part of a change looking finished.

* **British spelling** in prose: *behaviour*, *authorisation*, *organisation*,
  *utilisation*, *licence*. (JSON field names mirroring GitHub's API stay
  American: `organization` in a webhook payload is correct as-is.)
* **Comments explain why, not what.** The interesting ones name the failure mode
  being designed out, or the trade-off taken. Follow that; do not narrate code.
* **Error and warning messages are written for a person to act on.** An operator
  who gets a 403 should be told which role they are missing. Findings say what
  to change; API errors carry a human message and a stable code.
* **No em dashes.** Do not write `—` anywhere in this repository: prose,
  docs, comments, error messages, UI strings, commit messages or pull request
  text. Use a comma, a colon, a semicolon or parentheses, or split the sentence.
  Do not use `--` as a stand-in either. `internal/docs/no_em_dash_test.go`
  fails the build on a spaced em dash, and `internal/docs/double_hyphen_test.go`
  on a file that gains a spaced `--`. Older code comments still carry about six
  thousand of the latter, and they go as their lines are rewritten, not in one
  sweep that would bury every file's history. The one exception is the UI's
  placeholder for an absent value, which is two hyphens: write it as `NO_VALUE`
  from `web/src/lib/format.ts`, never as a dash of your own;
  `web/unit/absent-value.test.ts` guards it.
* **Diagrams are Mermaid**, in a `mermaid` fenced block beside the prose they
  explain, never ASCII art. The site renders them (`mkdocs.yml` registers the
  fence) and so does GitHub, so a diagram lives in the Markdown it belongs to and
  there is no exported image to go stale. Do not colour one by hand: Material
  themes it for light and dark, and a hard-coded fill is wrong in one of them.
* **Commit messages are imperative sentences in plain prose**, sentence case, no
  Conventional Commits prefix: *"Say why a pool has no host, and let a host say
  it can run again"*, *"Make both halves of 'no capacity' something an operator
  can do"*.

# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct

## Our pledge

We as members, contributors, and maintainers pledge to make participation in
the Zoomies community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of
age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex
characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience,
education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race,
religion, or sexual identity and orientation.

We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming,
diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.

## Our standards

Examples of behaviour that contributes to a positive environment for our
community include:

- Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
- Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
- Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
- Accepting responsibility and apologising to those affected by our mistakes,
  and learning from the experience
- Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall
  community

Examples of unacceptable behaviour include:

- The use of sexualised language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances
  of any kind
- Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political
  attacks
- Public or private harassment
- Publishing another person's private information, such as a physical or email
  address, without their explicit permission
- Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a
  professional setting

## Enforcement responsibilities

Zoomies maintainers are responsible for clarifying and enforcing these
standards of acceptable behaviour. They will take appropriate and fair
corrective action in response to behaviour they consider inappropriate,
threatening, offensive, or harmful.

Maintainers have the right and responsibility to remove, edit, or reject
comments, commits, code, documentation, issues, and other contributions that
are not aligned with this Code of Conduct. They will communicate reasons for
moderation decisions when appropriate.

## Scope

This Code of Conduct applies in all Zoomies community spaces. It also applies
when an individual is officially representing the project in public spaces.

Examples of representing the project include using an official project email
address, posting through an official social media account, or acting as an
appointed representative at an online or offline event.

## Enforcement

Report abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behaviour privately
through the repository's
[private reporting form](https://github.com/eyupio/zoomies/security/advisories/new).
Begin the report title with `Code of Conduct:` so it can be routed correctly.
Although GitHub labels this form as a security advisory, Zoomies also uses it
for confidential conduct reports because its contents are visible only to the
reporter and repository maintainers.

Include links, screenshots, dates, and other context that may help the
maintainers understand what happened. Do not include sensitive information
that is not necessary to investigate the report.

All reports will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly. Maintainers
will respect the privacy and security of the reporter and will share details
only with people needed to investigate and resolve the matter.

If a report concerns a maintainer who would normally receive it, or you do not
feel safe using the project channel, use
[GitHub's reporting tools](https://support.github.com/contact/report-abuse).

## Enforcement guidelines

Maintainers will follow these Community Impact Guidelines when determining the
consequences for an action they consider to violate this Code of Conduct.

### 1. Correction

**Community impact:** Use of inappropriate language or other behaviour deemed
unprofessional or unwelcome in the community.

**Consequence:** A private written warning from maintainers, providing clarity
about the violation and explaining why the behaviour was inappropriate. A
public apology may be requested.

### 2. Warning

**Community impact:** A violation through a single incident or series of
actions.

**Consequence:** A warning with consequences for continued behaviour. The
person responsible may be required to avoid interaction with the people
involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing this Code of
Conduct, for a specified period. This includes interactions in project spaces
and external channels such as social media. Violating these terms may lead to a
temporary or permanent ban.

### 3. Temporary ban

**Community impact:** A serious violation of community standards, including
sustained inappropriate behaviour.

**Consequence:** A temporary ban from interaction or public communication with
the community for a specified period. No public or private interaction with the
people involved, including unsolicited interaction with those enforcing this
Code of Conduct, is allowed during that period. Violating these terms may lead
to a permanent ban.

### 4. Permanent ban

**Community impact:** Demonstrating a pattern of violating community standards,
including sustained inappropriate behaviour, harassment of an individual, or
aggression toward or disparagement of classes of individuals.

**Consequence:** A permanent ban from public interaction within the Zoomies
community.

## Attribution

This Code of Conduct is adapted from the
[Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org), version 2.0,
available at
https://www.contributor-covenant.org/version/2/0/code_of_conduct.html.

The Community Impact Guidelines were inspired by
[Mozilla's code of conduct enforcement ladder](https://github.com/mozilla/diversity).

Answers to common questions about the Contributor Covenant are available in its
[FAQ](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/faq), with
[translations](https://www.contributor-covenant.org/translations) also
