COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-entrypoint.sh /usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-inventory.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-inventory.sh

# What this image is, for the entrypoint's first log line and for a job that
# wants to branch on it. A pool pointed at the wrong variant otherwise shows up
# as a missing package several minutes into a workflow.
ENV ZOOMIES_RUNNER_OS="${OS_ID}" \
    ZOOMIES_RUNNER_OS_VERSION="${OS_VERSION}" \
    ZOOMIES_RUNNER_VERSION="${RUNNER_VERSION}"

RUN mkdir -p /usr/local/share/zoomies && /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-inventory.sh > /usr/local/share/zoomies/installed-software.json
USER runner
ENV RUNNER_ALLOW_RUNASROOT=0
ENTRYPOINT ["/usr/local/bin/entrypoint.sh"]


# --- runner-docker ------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The Docker CLI, buildx and compose, for pools whose docker_mode is dind or
# host-socket. Only the client: the daemon is the pool's business, and this
# image never starts one.
#
# From Docker's own apt repository rather than Ubuntu's docker.io package,
# because that one drags in the daemon, containerd and runc -- a few hundred MB
# of software this image must never run.
FROM runner-base AS runner-docker
ARG OS_FAMILY
ARG OS_ID
USER root

COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-dnf.sh /tmp/
COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-apt.sh deploy/runner-docker-cli.sh /tmp/
RUN /tmp/runner-docker-cli.sh "${OS_FAMILY}" "${OS_ID}" && rm /tmp/runner-docker-cli.sh /tmp/runner-apt.sh /tmp/runner-dnf.sh
# Prove the client landed somewhere the runner will actually find it: a plugin
# installed but unreachable is the same failure as no client at all, and it is
# far cheaper to catch here than in somebody's workflow.
RUN set -eux; \
    docker --version; \
    docker buildx version
RUN mkdir -p /usr/local/share/zoomies && /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-inventory.sh > /usr/local/share/zoomies/installed-software.json
USER runner

# Stamp the finished image without invalidating its Docker CLI installation.
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG COMMIT=""
ARG DATE=""
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="zoomies-runner-docker" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="GitHub Actions runner image for Zoomies, with the Docker CLI" \
      org.opencontainers.image.version="${VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.revision="${COMMIT}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.created="${DATE}"


# --- runner-full --------------------------------------------------------------
#
# runner-docker plus the language toolchains the setup-* actions would
# otherwise download at the start of every job: Python, Node.js, Go and Java in
# the tool cache, laid out exactly as setup-python, setup-node, setup-go and
# setup-java look for them, and .NET, Maven, Gradle and Rust where a workflow
# finds them without a setup action. Which releases is deploy/toolcache.lock,
# every archive pinned by digest; deploy/runner-toolcache.sh is how each one
# lands.
#
# Published as ghcr.io/eyupio/zoomies-runner-full, for the Ubuntu variants
# only: the Python builds setup-python installs are made for Ubuntu and nothing
# else, and a full image without them would be the one toolchain most jobs ask
# for first. It is built on runner-docker because a pool that wants a build
# environment wants to build images in it too, and the client is a rounding
# error beside the rest.
#
# One layer per toolchain, so a lock change that moves one Node patch rebuilds
# that layer and not the other several gigabytes.
FROM runner-docker AS runner-full
ARG OS_VERSION
ARG TARGETARCH
USER root

# Rust's homes are fixed paths rather than the runner's ~/.cargo, so that the
# image can put them on PATH; the runner owns them, so rustup can still add a
# toolchain a workflow asks for.
ENV RUSTUP_HOME=/usr/local/rustup \
    CARGO_HOME=/usr/local/cargo

COPY --chmod=0755 deploy/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh
COPY deploy/toolcache.lock /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" python \
    && chown -R runner:runner "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY}/Python"
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" node \
    && chown -R runner:runner "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY}/node"
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" go \
    && chown -R runner:runner "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY}/go"
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" java \
    && chown -R runner:runner "${AGENT_TOOLSDIRECTORY}/Java_Temurin-Hotspot_jdk"
# setup-dotnet installs into /usr/share/dotnet as the runner, so the runner
# owns it; otherwise asking for an SDK the image lacks fails on permissions.
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" dotnet \
    && chown -R runner:runner /usr/share/dotnet
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" maven \
    && /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" gradle
RUN /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-toolcache.sh /usr/local/lib/zoomies/toolcache.lock "${OS_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" rustup \
    && chown -R runner:runner "${RUSTUP_HOME}" "${CARGO_HOME}"

# JDK 17 is the default GitHub's Ubuntu runners give a job that does not ask,
# and the same here; setup-java replaces it for one that does. Maven and Gradle
# need a JAVA_HOME before either will start.
ENV JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/temurin-17 \
    PATH=/usr/local/cargo/bin:/usr/lib/jvm/temurin-17/bin:${PATH} \
    DOTNET_ROOT=/usr/share/dotnet \
    DOTNET_NOLOGO=1 \
    DOTNET_CLI_TELEMETRY_OPTOUT=1 \
    DOTNET_SKIP_FIRST_TIME_EXPERIENCE=1

# Prove each toolchain answers from where a job will look for it, as the
# other targets do for theirs.
RUN set -eux; \
    java -version; \
    mvn --version; \
    gradle --version --no-daemon; \
    dotnet --list-sdks; \
    rustc --version; \
    cargo --version; \
    cargo clippy --version; \
    rustfmt --version
RUN mkdir -p /usr/local/share/zoomies && /usr/local/lib/zoomies/runner-inventory.sh > /usr/local/share/zoomies/installed-software.json
USER runner

ARG VERSION=dev
ARG COMMIT=""
ARG DATE=""
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.title="zoomies-runner-full" \
      org.opencontainers.image.description="GitHub Actions runner image for Zoomies, with the Docker CLI and the language toolchains setup-* actions install" \
      org.opencontainers.image.version="${VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.revision="${COMMIT}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.created="${DATE}"


# --- runner -------------------------------------------------------------------
#
# The default target: the runner and the build toolchain, without the Docker
# client. Last in the file so that a bare build with no --target produces it.
FROM runner-base AS runner
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG COMMIT=""
ARG DATE=""
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.version="${VERSION}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.revision="${COMMIT}" \
      org.opencontainers.image.created="${DATE}"

# The demo organisation's workflows

The public demo needs something for its fleet to do. These are the workflows
the `zoomies-demo` GitHub organisation runs, kept here so they are reviewed
with the rest of the demo. Nothing in this repository runs them: copy them
into the organisation's repositories. `docs/instapods.md` covers the fleet
itself, and `roadmap/plans/2026-10-12-public-demo-design.md` the reasons.

| File | Copy it to | What visitors see |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `build.yml` | every demo repository | lint, then build, then three test suites side by side, then package; one run in seven fails its end-to-end suite on purpose |
| `long-job.yml` | one demo repository | an eight-minute job, so there is nearly always a busy runner and a live log |
| `keepalive.yml` | every demo repository | nothing: it runs on GitHub's own runners, weekly |

Each goes in the repository's `.github/workflows/` under the same name.

## Before anything runs

The demo's runners are processes on a pod, not throwaway containers, and
everyone can read their logs. So the organisation is set up to run only its
own code and to hold nothing worth stealing.

1. **Create the organisation** (`zoomies-demo`) on GitHub's free plan, and a
   few public repositories with a little content each, so a checkout has
   something to fetch. Three is enough: `storefront`, `payments-api` and
   `docs-site`, say.
2. **Organisation settings, Actions, General:**
   * *Actions permissions*: allow actions created by GitHub only. The
     templates use `actions/checkout` and the `gh` command and nothing else.
   * *Approval for running fork pull request workflows*: require approval for
     **all outside collaborators**. None of these workflows runs on a pull
     request, but a pull request can add a workflow of its own that names the
     demo's label. Kennel Club warns (`exposure.fork_approval_weak`) about
     anything weaker.
   * *Workflow permissions*: read repository contents only. Each template
     declares its own permissions as well.
3. **No secrets and no variables**, in the organisation or any repository.
   Anyone reading the fleet reads every log.
4. **Install the GitHub App** from the controller (**Installations, Connect
   GitHub**) on the demo repositories only. On its first connection Zoomies
   creates a `zoomies` runner group that allows public repositories; leave
   it, because GitHub's Default group refuses public repositories.
5. **Create the pool** the templates ask for, `runs-on: zoomies-demo`, on the
   worker pod's process backend:

   ```sh
   zoomies pools create --name demo --labels zoomies-demo \
     --backend process --installation <id> --max 2
   ```

   The maximum is the worker's slots, as the Hosts page shows them.

## Spread the schedules

Every repository's `build.yml` ships with the same minutes. Change them per
repository so the runs take turns instead of queueing together:

| Repository | `build.yml` cron | Also carries |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `storefront` | `5,25,45 * * * *` | `long-job.yml` at `35 * * * *` |
| `payments-api` | `12,32,52 * * * *` | |
| `docs-site` | `18,38,58 * * * *` | |

With a two-slot worker that keeps the fleet busy most of the hour without a
queue that never drains. Each `build.yml` run is six jobs and about four
minutes of wall-clock time, and a run still waiting when the next is due is
replaced by it rather than stacked behind it.

GitHub disables scheduled workflows in a repository with no activity for
sixty days. `keepalive.yml` re-enables every workflow in its repository each
week, which resets that clock; it needs nothing from you but to be there.

# The demo fleet's busiest workflow: a pull-request-shaped pipeline that runs
# on a schedule instead. Copy it into a zoomies-demo repository as
# .github/workflows/build.yml; README.md in this folder says how the
# organisation around it has to be set up first.
#
# Every step is plain shell, because the demo's runners are processes on a
# pod (the process backend) with only what Ubuntu ships, and a demo that
# spends its minutes installing toolchains shows visitors a download bar.
# What it does show is the shape the fleet is for: a lint gate, a build, a
# test matrix running side by side, and a package step that waits for all
# of it.
name: build

on:
  schedule:
    # Every twenty minutes. Offset the minutes per repository (README.md has
    # a table) so the repositories take turns rather than queue together.
    - cron: "5,25,45 * * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

# Nothing here writes, and nothing a visitor can read should be able to.
permissions:
  contents: read

# One run at a time per repository. A run still queued when the next is due
# is replaced by it, so a slow afternoon never piles up a backlog.
concurrency:
  group: build
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: zoomies-demo
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Check formatting
        run: |
          echo "checking $(git ls-files | wc -l) tracked files"
          sleep 8
          echo "formatting: clean"
      - name: Static analysis
        run: |
          for pkg in api auth billing cart catalogue checkout search; do
            echo "analysing ./$pkg"
            sleep 2
          done
          echo "0 findings"

  build:
    needs: lint
    runs-on: zoomies-demo
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Compile
        run: |
          for unit in core storage http ui cli; do
            echo "compiling $unit"
            sleep 6
          done
          mkdir -p dist
          date -u +"built %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ by run ${GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER}" > dist/BUILD
          cat dist/BUILD

  test:
    needs: build
    runs-on: zoomies-demo
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      # Every suite reports even when one fails, so the failure views have a
      # red job beside green ones rather than a cancelled column.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        suite: [unit, integration, e2e]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Run the ${{ matrix.suite }} suite
        env:
          SUITE: ${{ matrix.suite }}
        run: |
          case "$SUITE" in
            unit) tests=48 pause=1 ;;
            integration) tests=16 pause=4 ;;
            e2e) tests=9 pause=8 ;;
          esac
          i=1
          while [ "$i" -le "$tests" ]; do
            printf 'ok   %s/test_%02d\n' "$SUITE" "$i"
            sleep "$pause"
            i=$((i + 1))
          done
          # One run in seven fails its end-to-end suite on purpose, so the
          # fleet always has a recent failure for visitors to open and for
          # Eli and the MCP tools to explain. It is labelled as planned in
          # the log, so nobody mistakes it for a broken demo.
          if [ "$SUITE" = e2e ] && [ $((GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER % 7)) -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "FAIL e2e/checkout_applies_discount: expected total 18.00, got 20.00"
            echo "(a planned failure: one run in seven fails here so the demo has one to show)"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "$tests passed"

  package:
    needs: test
    runs-on: zoomies-demo
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Package
        run: |
          echo "packaging run ${GITHUB_RUN_NUMBER}"
          sleep 10
          echo "package ready (not published: this is a demo)"

# Keeps the scheduled workflows above from being switched off. Copy it into
# every zoomies-demo repository as .github/workflows/keepalive.yml.
#
# GitHub disables a repository's scheduled workflows after sixty days with no
# activity in it, and a demo repository has no reason to change. Enabling a
# workflow again through the API resets that clock, so once a week this
# enables every workflow in its own repository, itself included.
#
# It runs on a GitHub-hosted runner, not the demo fleet, on purpose: it holds
# a token that can change this repository's Actions settings, and the demo's
# runners are processes on a shared pod whose logs anyone can read. The token
# is the job's own GITHUB_TOKEN, so the organisation still holds no secret.
name: keepalive

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "17 4 * * 1"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  actions: write

jobs:
  enable:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 5
    steps:
      - name: Enable every workflow in this repository
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
        run: |
          gh api "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows" --jq '.workflows[].id' |
            while read -r id; do
              gh api -X PUT "repos/$REPO/actions/workflows/$id/enable"
              echo "enabled workflow $id"
            done

# A job that takes long enough to watch. Copy it into one zoomies-demo
# repository as .github/workflows/long-job.yml.
#
# Most of the demo's jobs finish in a minute or two, which is how a fleet
# should look, but it means a visitor who arrives between runs sees nothing
# moving. This one runs for about eight minutes with steady output, so there
# is nearly always a busy runner and a log that is still being written.
name: long job

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "35 * * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: long-job
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  soak:
    runs-on: zoomies-demo
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
      - name: Soak test
        run: |
          step=1
          while [ "$step" -le 48 ]; do
            printf 'soak %2d/48: %d requests, p95 %d ms\n' "$step" $((step * 250)) $((40 + step % 9))
            sleep 10
            step=$((step + 1))
          done
          echo "soak complete"

#!/bin/sh
# The Build command of a Zoomies pod on InstaPods (see docs/instapods.md):
#
#   sh deploy/instapods/fetch.sh controller   on the web pod
#   sh deploy/instapods/fetch.sh agent        on the worker pod
#
# The role can come from ZOOMIES_POD_ROLE instead of the argument, exactly as
# it can for run.sh, so one variable set on the pod keeps the two in step.
#
# It downloads a published release rather than building one. The Go preset
# carries an older Go than go.mod asks for and no Node at all, and the UI is
# built with Node before the Go build can embed it; a release binary is also
# the very file every other install runs, checked against the same
# checksums.txt the installer checks it against.
#
# The binary goes to $HOME/zoomies/bin, outside the git checkout, so the pull
# at the start of every deploy can never clobber it, and a failed build leaves
# the one that was running in place.

set -eu

REPO=eyupio/zoomies
BASE_URL="https://github.com/${REPO}/releases"
BIN_DIR="$HOME/zoomies/bin"
BIN="$BIN_DIR/zoomies"

# The checkout this script sits in: deploy/instapods/ is two levels down.
APP_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
# shellcheck source=deploy/instapods/lib.sh
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

say() { printf 'zoomies: %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf 'zoomies: warning: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

fetch() {
    # fetch <url> <dest>
    if have curl; then
        curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 -o "$2" "$1"
    elif have wget; then
        wget -qO "$2" "$1"
    else
        die "neither curl nor wget is on this pod, and one is needed to download Zoomies."
    fi
}

# --- release signature check: identical in connect-proxmox.sh and
# --- deploy/instapods/fetch.sh, and a test in internal/docs holds the copies equal.
# The release signing key, base64: the line `zoomies release keygen` writes to
# release.pub. A test keeps it equal to the key compiled into the binary and to
# the one in install.sh, and keeps the two functions below identical in every
# script that carries them.
RELEASE_KEY="6dK2/jDPHR8wAjsIayrxGxL8ednKVKdEMHdRcmNU67U="

# signature_required says whether a release has to carry a signature. The first
# signed release was v1.3.6.1: everything before it has none, so there is
# nothing to check and refusing them would refuse every version published before
# signing began, and the moving dev prerelease is never signed. From v1.3.6 up a
# release that is not signed is refused, because otherwise whoever could replace
# the binary could also delete its signature, and a script that only warns would
# run what is left.
#
# A name this cannot read as three short numbers is held to a signature as well.
# Whoever publishes a release picks its name, so a name nobody can place must
# never be the way out of the check. A number is compared only when it is short
# enough to compare: the shell's [ answers one that overflows with an error
# status, which a caller would read as "not required".
signature_required() {
    [ "$1" != dev ] || return 1
    case "$1" in v[0-9]*.[0-9]*.[0-9]*) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
    _rest=${1#v}
    _major=${_rest%%.*}
    _rest=${_rest#*.}
    _minor=${_rest%%.*}
    _rest=${_rest#*.}
    _patch=${_rest%%[!0-9]*}
    for _n in "$_major" "$_minor" "$_patch"; do
        case $_n in [0-9] | [0-9][0-9] | [0-9][0-9][0-9] | [0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]) ;; *) return 0 ;; esac
    done
    [ "$_major" -gt 1 ] || { [ "$_major" -eq 1 ] && { [ "$_minor" -gt 3 ] || { [ "$_minor" -eq 3 ] && [ "$_patch" -gt 5 ]; }; }; }
}

# verify_signature <tag> <checksums.txt> <checksums.txt.ed25519> <scratch dir>
# holds a release's checksums to the release key, before the checksums are
# believed. A signature that does not match always refuses. A signature that
# cannot be checked (no openssl that does Ed25519, no signature, one that cannot
# be read) refuses a release that must be signed and is a warning for one that
# cannot be, which is every release before v1.3.6.
verify_signature() {
    _tag=$1 _sums=$2 _sigfile=$3 _dir=$4
    [ -n "$RELEASE_KEY" ] || return 0
    if ! command -v openssl >/dev/null 2>&1 || ! openssl pkeyutl -help 2>&1 | grep -q rawin; then
        if signature_required "$_tag"; then
            die "$_tag is signed, and this host has no openssl (3.0 or later) to check the signature with, so the download cannot be trusted. Install openssl and run this again."
        fi
        warn "there is no openssl here that can check a signature; this download is checked by its checksum alone."
        return 0
    fi
    if [ ! -s "$_sigfile" ]; then
        if signature_required "$_tag"; then
            die "$_tag carries no checksums.txt.ed25519, and a release this new must be signed. Do not run this download."
        fi
        warn "$_tag carries no checksums.txt.ed25519, so the release key cannot check it; this download is checked by its checksum alone."
        return 0
    fi
    # The envelope is the key id, then the base64 signature.
    _sig=$(sed -n '2p' "$_sigfile")
    if ! printf '%s' "$_sig" | openssl base64 -d -A > "$_dir/sig.raw" 2>/dev/null || [ ! -s "$_dir/sig.raw" ]; then
        if signature_required "$_tag"; then
            die "the signature on $_tag could not be read. Do not run this download."
        fi
        warn "the release signature could not be read; this download is checked by its checksum alone."
        return 0
    fi
    # openssl wants the DER public key: the fixed Ed25519 SubjectPublicKeyInfo
    # prefix, then the key's 32 bytes. While a key is rotated RELEASE_KEY holds
    # more than one, one per line, exactly as the binary's key set does, and the
    # signature has to verify under one of them.
    printf '\060\052\060\005\006\003\053\145\160\003\041\000' > "$_dir/key.prefix"
    printf '%s\n' "$RELEASE_KEY" > "$_dir/keys.txt"
    _keys=0 _matched=0
    while IFS= read -r _key; do
        _key=$(printf '%s' "$_key" | tr -d '[:space:]')
        [ -n "$_key" ] || continue
        _keys=$((_keys + 1))
        if ! printf '%s' "$_key" | openssl base64 -d -A > "$_dir/key.raw" 2>/dev/null || [ ! -s "$_dir/key.raw" ]; then
            die "the release key built into this script cannot be read; copy the script again from https://zoomies.sh."
        fi
        cat "$_dir/key.prefix" "$_dir/key.raw" > "$_dir/release.der"
        if openssl pkeyutl -verify -pubin -keyform DER -inkey "$_dir/release.der" \
            -rawin -in "$_sums" -sigfile "$_dir/sig.raw" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            _matched=1
            break
        fi
    done < "$_dir/keys.txt"
    [ "$_keys" -gt 0 ] || die "the release key built into this script cannot be read; copy the script again from https://zoomies.sh."
    if [ "$_matched" -eq 1 ]; then
        say "the release signature matches the release key"
    else
        die "the release signature on $_tag does not match the release key. Do not run this download."
    fi
}
# --- end of the release signature check.

sha256_of() {
    if have sha256sum; then
        sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    elif have shasum; then
        shasum -a 256 "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else
        printf ''
    fi
}

# resolve_latest names the tag /releases/latest redirects to. While every
# release is a prerelease GitHub redirects to the release index instead, so
# the newest v-tag from the API is the fallback; the moving dev prerelease is
# never what "latest" means.
resolve_latest() {
    url=''
    if have curl; then
        url=$(curl -fsSLI -o /dev/null -w '%{url_effective}' "$BASE_URL/latest" 2>/dev/null || printf '')
    fi
    case "$url" in
        */tag/*)
            printf '%s\n' "${url##*/tag/}"
            return 0
            ;;
    esac
    api="https://api.github.com/repos/${REPO}/releases?per_page=20"
    body=$(curl -fsSL "$api" 2>/dev/null || printf '')
    printf '%s\n' "$body" | grep -o '"tag_name"[^,]*' |
        sed 's/.*: *"//; s/".*//' | grep '^v' | head -1
}

# as_root runs a command as root: directly when this already is root, through
# sudo when sudo needs no password, and not at all otherwise. A Build command
# has no terminal, so a sudo that asks for a password would hang the deploy
# instead of failing it.
as_root() {
    if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
        "$@"
    else
        sudo -n "$@"
    fi
}

# runner_libraries makes sure the native libraries actions/runner loads are
# installed. The process backend runs the runner straight on this pod, with no
# image to bring them, and a runner missing libicu exits at startup with an
# error that names .NET rather than the package. The names are Ubuntu 24.04's,
# which is what a pod runs.
runner_libraries() {
    set -- libicu74 libkrb5-3 zlib1g libssl3t64 liblttng-ust1t64
    if ! have dpkg-query; then
        warn "this is not a Debian or Ubuntu system, so the runner's libraries were not checked." \
            "The process backend needs ICU, Kerberos, zlib, OpenSSL and LTTng-UST installed."
        return 0
    fi
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091 # the system's file, read for two fields
    release=$(. /etc/os-release 2>/dev/null && printf '%s %s' "${ID:-}" "${VERSION_ID:-}" || printf '')
    if [ "$release" != "ubuntu 24.04" ]; then
        warn "the runner's library names here are Ubuntu 24.04's and this is ${release:-an unknown release}." \
            "If a runner exits at startup, install what actions/runner's bin/installdependencies.sh lists."
        return 0
    fi
    missing=''
    for pkg in "$@"; do
        # shellcheck disable=SC2016 # ${Status} is dpkg-query's format, not ours
        status=$(dpkg-query -W -f='${Status}' "$pkg" 2>/dev/null || printf '')
        case "$status" in
            *' installed') ;;
            *) missing="$missing $pkg" ;;
        esac
    done
    missing=${missing# }
    if [ -z "$missing" ]; then
        say "the runner's libraries are installed"
        return 0
    fi
    if [ "$(id -u)" -ne 0 ] && ! sudo -n true 2>/dev/null; then
        die "the GitHub Actions runner needs packages this pod does not have: $missing" \
            "This user cannot run sudo without a password, so install them from the pod's" \
            "Web Terminal or over SSH, then deploy again:" \
            "  sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y $missing"
    fi
    say "installing the runner's libraries: $missing"
    # Word splitting is the point: $missing is a list of package names.
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    if ! { as_root env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get update -qq &&
        as_root env DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends $missing; }; then
        die "installing $missing failed (the apt-get output is above)." \
            "Install them from the pod's Web Terminal, then deploy again:" \
            "  sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y $missing"
    fi
}

# write_launcher puts a small script at the path the Go preset's service runs
# when no Start command is in force. The preset documents that its service
# runs $APP_DIR/app; the Start command this guide sets is meant to replace
# that, and this keeps a pod whose Start command was cleared or never saved
# running the right role instead of a missing file.
write_launcher() {
    launcher="$APP_DIR/app"
    if [ -e "$launcher" ] && [ ! -f "$launcher" ]; then
        warn "$launcher exists and is not a file, so no launcher was written there."
        return 0
    fi
    tmp_launcher="$launcher.zoomies.$$"
    cat >"$tmp_launcher" <<EOF
#!/bin/sh
# Written by deploy/instapods/fetch.sh on every deploy; edits here are lost.
exec sh "$APP_DIR/deploy/instapods/run.sh" $ROLE "\$@"
EOF
    chmod 0755 "$tmp_launcher"
    mv -f "$tmp_launcher" "$launcher"
}

load_env "$APP_DIR/.env"

ROLE=${1:-${ZOOMIES_POD_ROLE:-}}
case "$ROLE" in
    controller | agent) ;;
    '') die "say which pod this is: sh deploy/instapods/fetch.sh controller (the web pod)" \
        "or sh deploy/instapods/fetch.sh agent (the worker pod), or set ZOOMIES_POD_ROLE." ;;
    *) die "$ROLE is not a role: use controller (the web pod) or agent (the worker pod)." ;;
esac

[ "$(uname -s)" = Linux ] || die "this script is for an InstaPods pod, which runs Linux."
case "$(uname -m)" in
    x86_64 | amd64) ARCH=amd64 ;;
    aarch64 | arm64) ARCH=arm64 ;;
    *) die "$(uname -m) is not an architecture Zoomies ships: there are amd64 and arm64 builds." ;;
esac
ASSET="zoomies_linux_${ARCH}"

VERSION=${ZOOMIES_VERSION:-latest}
if [ "$VERSION" = latest ]; then
    TAG=$(resolve_latest)
    [ -n "$TAG" ] || die "could not work out which release is the latest." \
        "Set ZOOMIES_VERSION to a tag (dev, or v1.2.3) with instapods env set, and deploy again."
    # GitHub's latest is the newest release by date, and whoever publishes a
    # release picks its name and can attach a checksums.txt that matches a
    # binary of their own. Every release from v1.3.6 up is signed, so a latest
    # that needs no signature is not one of ours, and is refused rather than
    # taken on its checksum with a warning. That leniency is for a release the
    # operator names, below, which is their choice; this one was not.
    signature_required "$TAG" ||
        die "the release GitHub calls the latest is named $TAG, which is not the name of a signed Zoomies release, so nothing was downloaded." \
            "Every release from v1.3.6 up is signed. This name belongs to an older one, to the moving dev prerelease, or to none of ours." \
            "Look at $BASE_URL to see what was published. If a release you trust is there, set ZOOMIES_VERSION to its tag" \
            "with instapods env set and deploy again. If you did not expect this, report it at https://github.com/${REPO}/issues."
else
    TAG=$VERSION
    # Numeric versions keep the project's v-prefixed tag spelling.
    case "$TAG" in dev | v*) ;; *) TAG="v$TAG" ;; esac
fi
say "release $TAG ($VERSION), $ASSET"

mkdir -p "$BIN_DIR"
WORK=$(mktemp -d "$BIN_DIR/.fetch.XXXXXX")
# shellcheck disable=SC2064 # expand now: the directory is fixed from here on
trap "rm -rf '$WORK'" EXIT
trap 'exit 1' INT TERM

# A download that cannot be verified is refused, never installed with a
# warning: a deploy log is not somewhere anybody reads a warning.
fetch "$BASE_URL/download/$TAG/checksums.txt" "$WORK/checksums.txt" ||
    die "could not download checksums.txt for $TAG." \
        "$BASE_URL/download/$TAG/checksums.txt" \
        "Check that $TAG exists at $BASE_URL. If it was published minutes ago its" \
        "binaries may still be uploading; deploy again shortly."
# A release before v1.3.6 has no signature; the file is simply absent then.
fetch "$BASE_URL/download/$TAG/checksums.txt.ed25519" "$WORK/checksums.txt.ed25519" 2>/dev/null ||
    rm -f "$WORK/checksums.txt.ed25519"
# Before the checksums are believed: a checksum from the same place as the binary
# says only that the download was not corrupted on the way.
verify_signature "$TAG" "$WORK/checksums.txt" "$WORK/checksums.txt.ed25519" "$WORK"
WANT=$(awk -v a="$ASSET" '$2 == a || $2 == "*"a {print $1; exit}' "$WORK/checksums.txt")
[ -n "$WANT" ] || die "checksums.txt for $TAG has no entry for $ASSET, so a download could not be verified." \
    "Choose another release with ZOOMIES_VERSION, and deploy again."

if [ -x "$BIN" ] && [ "$(sha256_of "$BIN")" = "$WANT" ]; then
    # Nothing to fetch: the same deploy run twice, or an env change that
    # did not move the version, should not cost a 40 MB download.
    say "already have $ASSET for $TAG"
else
    fetch "$BASE_URL/download/$TAG/$ASSET" "$WORK/zoomies" ||
        die "could not download $ASSET for $TAG from $BASE_URL/download/$TAG/$ASSET." \
            "Check that the release exists and has finished uploading, then deploy again."
    GOT=$(sha256_of "$WORK/zoomies")
    [ -n "$GOT" ] || die "there is no sha256sum or shasum on this pod to check the download with."
    if [ "$GOT" != "$WANT" ]; then
        die "checksum mismatch for $ASSET $TAG: the download is not what the release published." \
            "expected $WANT" \
            "got      $GOT" \
            "It was not installed, and the binary already here was left alone. Deploy again," \
            "and if it happens twice, report it at https://github.com/${REPO}/issues."
    fi
    chmod 0755 "$WORK/zoomies"
    # Running it once catches a binary that cannot execute here before it
    # replaces one that can.
    "$WORK/zoomies" version >/dev/null 2>&1 ||
        die "the downloaded $ASSET does not run on this pod; the binary already here was left alone."
    # A rename within one directory is atomic, and a running process keeps
    # the file it started from, so the service is never left without one.
    mv -f "$WORK/zoomies" "$BIN"
    say "sha256 $(printf '%.12s' "$GOT")... matches; installed $BIN"
fi

if [ "$ROLE" = agent ]; then
    runner_libraries
fi

write_launcher
"$BIN" version | head -1 | sed 's/^/zoomies: ready: /'

#!/bin/sh
# The Start command of a Zoomies pod on InstaPods (see docs/instapods.md):
#
#   sh deploy/instapods/run.sh controller   on the web pod
#   sh deploy/instapods/run.sh agent        on the worker pod
#
# The role can come from ZOOMIES_POD_ROLE instead of the argument, as it can
# for fetch.sh. Everything here is a default: a ZOOMIES_* variable set with
# `instapods env set` wins over it, and the binary is the one fetch.sh put in
# $HOME/zoomies/bin during the Build step.

set -eu

APP_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
# shellcheck source=deploy/instapods/lib.sh
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

load_env "$APP_DIR/.env"

ROLE=${1:-${ZOOMIES_POD_ROLE:-}}
case "$ROLE" in
    controller | agent) ;;
    '') die "say which pod this is: sh deploy/instapods/run.sh controller (the web pod)" \
        "or sh deploy/instapods/run.sh agent (the worker pod), or set ZOOMIES_POD_ROLE." ;;
    *) die "$ROLE is not a role: use controller (the web pod) or agent (the worker pod)." ;;
esac

# ZOOMIES_BIN points this at another binary, for trying a build of your own
# on the pod without publishing it.
ZOOMIES_BIN=${ZOOMIES_BIN:-$HOME/zoomies/bin/zoomies}
[ -x "$ZOOMIES_BIN" ] || die "there is no Zoomies binary at $ZOOMIES_BIN." \
    "The Build command (sh deploy/instapods/fetch.sh $ROLE) downloads it there;" \
    "read the last deploy's build log for why it did not, and deploy again."

# Both pods keep everything under $HOME/zoomies, beside the binary and outside
# the git checkout, so a redeploy's pull never touches the database, the
# encryption key or the agent's credentials. Pointing ZOOMIES_CONFIG_DIR there
# too means the default zoomies.yaml path is one this user owns: the file need
# not exist, and environment variables alone configure the process.
: "${ZOOMIES_STATE_DIR:=$HOME/zoomies/data}"
: "${ZOOMIES_CONFIG_DIR:=$HOME/zoomies/data}"
: "${ZOOMIES_LOG_FORMAT:=text}"
export ZOOMIES_STATE_DIR ZOOMIES_CONFIG_DIR ZOOMIES_LOG_FORMAT
# The controller opens its database lock without creating the folder first,
# which an installer or a mounted volume normally has. Private to this user:
# the folder holds the database and, unless one is supplied, the key.
(umask 077 && mkdir -p "$ZOOMIES_STATE_DIR" "$ZOOMIES_CONFIG_DIR")

case "$ROLE" in
    controller)
        # InstaPods proxies the pod's https address to the port in $PORT
        # (8080) and holds the certificate, so the controller listens in the
        # clear on every interface and says so at startup; behind this proxy
        # that warning is expected.
        : "${ZOOMIES_BIND:=0.0.0.0:${PORT:-8080}}"
        : "${ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE:=off}"
        # A pod has no Docker, so an agent inside the controller could never
        # start a runner. Runners come from the worker pod, which also keeps
        # every job away from the database and the GitHub App's key.
        : "${ZOOMIES_AGENT_EMBEDDED:=false}"
        export ZOOMIES_BIND ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE ZOOMIES_AGENT_EMBEDDED
        exec "$ZOOMIES_BIN" controller
        ;;
    agent)
        # No Docker on a pod, so each runner is a process in it: see the
        # process backend in docs/security.md for what that means.
        : "${ZOOMIES_AGENT_BACKEND:=process}"
        : "${ZOOMIES_WORK_DIR:=$HOME/zoomies/work}"
        export ZOOMIES_AGENT_BACKEND ZOOMIES_WORK_DIR
        [ -n "${ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_URL:-}" ] ||
            die "ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_URL is not set. Set it to the web pod's https address:" \
                "  instapods env set <worker-pod> ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_URL=https://<web-pod>.<region>.instapods.app" \
                "It stays set: the agent reads it on every start, not only the first."
        # The agent keeps the credentials it was given when it joined in
        # agent.json in its work directory. Only a pod without them needs a
        # join token, and a token is single use, so asking for one here would
        # be wrong on every start after the first.
        if [ ! -s "$ZOOMIES_WORK_DIR/agent.json" ] && [ -z "${ZOOMIES_JOIN_TOKEN:-}" ]; then
            die "this pod has not joined the controller yet, and ZOOMIES_JOIN_TOKEN is not set." \
                "Mint a join token on the controller (Hosts, then Add a host, or" \
                "zoomies hosts join-token create --ttl 15m) and give it to this pod:" \
                "  instapods env set <worker-pod> ZOOMIES_JOIN_TOKEN=zoojoin_..." \
                "It is needed once: the credentials it buys are kept in $ZOOMIES_WORK_DIR/agent.json."
        fi
        exec "$ZOOMIES_BIN" agent
        ;;
esac

#!/bin/sh
# Brings a Zoomies pod on InstaPods up to date (see docs/instapods.md):
#
#   sh deploy/instapods/update.sh             this pod, now
#   sh deploy/instapods/update.sh --force     the worker, even with a job running
#   sh deploy/instapods/update.sh controller  name the role when it cannot be told
#
# It does what the dashboard's Deploy does, for a pod that has no Deploy button:
# it moves the checkout to the newest commit, runs the Build command
# (fetch.sh, which downloads the release the pod's ZOOMIES_VERSION names and
# checks it against the release's checksums) and restarts the app. The controller
# pod has a Deploy button and can use that instead; this works on both, so one
# command keeps the pair in step.
#
# Nothing is restarted when nothing changed, so it is safe to run on a schedule.
#
# The checkout is reset to the remote's commit, so a hand edit to a tracked file
# in ~/app is discarded. The environment file, the database, the encryption key
# and the agent's credentials are not in the checkout and are never touched.

set -eu

APP_DIR=$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../.." && pwd)
# shellcheck source=deploy/instapods/lib.sh
. "$(dirname "$0")/lib.sh"

say() { printf 'zoomies: %s\n' "$*"; }
warn() { printf 'zoomies: warning: %s\n' "$*" >&2; }
have() { command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1; }

# sha_of is empty for a file that is not there, which is what "nothing
# installed yet" should compare as.
sha_of() {
    if [ -f "$1" ]; then
        sha256sum "$1" | cut -d' ' -f1
    else
        printf ''
    fi
}

# job_running says whether the Actions runner has a job in progress. A job runs
# in a Runner.Worker process the runner starts for it, and restarting the agent
# kills that process and fails the job. The bracket keeps this very command line
# from matching its own pattern.
job_running() {
    grep -qa 'Runner[.]Worker' /proc/[0-9]*/cmdline 2>/dev/null
}

# job_blocks_restart <role> <force> says whether a restart now would fail a job:
# this is the worker, --force was not given, and a job is in progress.
job_blocks_restart() {
    [ "$1" = agent ] && [ "$2" -eq 0 ] && job_running
}

# restart_app restarts the pod's app service, and returns 1 when there is no
# service here to restart, so that the caller does not claim the new version is
# running. reset-failed first, because a service that crashed on its way down (a
# missing token, say) can be refused a restart for starting too often.
restart_app() {
    if ! have systemctl || ! systemctl cat app.service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        say "restart the app to run the new version: sudo systemctl restart app"
        return 1
    fi
    if [ "$(id -u)" -eq 0 ]; then
        systemctl reset-failed app 2>/dev/null || true
        systemctl restart app
    elif sudo -n true 2>/dev/null; then
        sudo -n systemctl reset-failed app 2>/dev/null || true
        sudo -n systemctl restart app
    else
        die "the new version is installed but the app was not restarted:" \
            "this user cannot run sudo without a password. Restart it from the" \
            "pod's Terminal or its dashboard:" \
            "  sudo systemctl restart app"
    fi
    sleep 3
    if ! systemctl is-active --quiet app; then
        die "the app did not stay up after the restart. Read why with:" \
            "  journalctl -u app -n 30 --no-pager"
    fi
    say "restarted the app"
}

# The whole script is one function, called on the same line that ends the file.
# A shell reads a script as it runs it, and the checkout reset below can replace
# this very file; a function is read in full before it runs, so the new contents
# are never half-read in the middle of the old ones.
main() {
    force=0
    role=''
    for arg in "$@"; do
        case "$arg" in
            --force) force=1 ;;
            controller | agent) role=$arg ;;
            *) die "$arg is not something this takes." \
                "usage: sh deploy/instapods/update.sh [--force] [controller|agent]" ;;
        esac
    done

    load_env "$APP_DIR/.env"

    # A pod that points at a controller is the worker; the web pod points at
    # nothing. ZOOMIES_POD_ROLE says so outright when it is set.
    if [ -z "$role" ]; then role=${ZOOMIES_POD_ROLE:-}; fi
    if [ -z "$role" ]; then
        if [ -n "${ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_URL:-}" ]; then
            role=agent
        else
            role=controller
        fi
    fi

    if job_blocks_restart "$role" "$force"; then
        say "a job is running here, and restarting would fail it, so nothing was changed."
        say "run this again when it has finished, or with --force to update anyway."
        return 0
    fi

    bin=${ZOOMIES_BIN:-$HOME/zoomies/bin/zoomies}
    # Written when a job holds a restart back, and read by the next run: with the
    # new binary already in place that run would otherwise find nothing to do,
    # and the app would go on running the old one.
    pending="$(dirname "$bin")/restart-pending"
    before_bin=$(sha_of "$bin")
    before_scripts=''

    if [ -d "$APP_DIR/.git" ]; then
        before_scripts=$(git -C "$APP_DIR" rev-parse HEAD:deploy/instapods 2>/dev/null || printf '')
        branch=$(git -C "$APP_DIR" symbolic-ref --short -q HEAD || printf 'main')
        say "moving the checkout to the newest $branch"
        git -C "$APP_DIR" fetch -q --depth 1 origin "$branch"
        git -C "$APP_DIR" reset -q --hard FETCH_HEAD
    else
        warn "$APP_DIR is not a git checkout, so its scripts were not updated."
    fi

    sh "$APP_DIR/deploy/instapods/fetch.sh" "$role"

    after_bin=$(sha_of "$bin")
    after_scripts=''
    if [ -d "$APP_DIR/.git" ]; then
        after_scripts=$(git -C "$APP_DIR" rev-parse HEAD:deploy/instapods 2>/dev/null || printf '')
    fi

    # The scripts are compared as well as the binary: they decide how the app
    # starts, but most commits to the repository change neither, and a pod that
    # restarted for every one of them would restart daily for nothing.
    if [ "$before_bin" = "$after_bin" ] && [ "$before_scripts" = "$after_scripts" ] && [ ! -e "$pending" ]; then
        say "already up to date; nothing was restarted."
        return 0
    fi

    # The check at the top was made before the download, and a download takes
    # minutes: a job that started in them would be failed by this restart.
    if job_blocks_restart "$role" "$force"; then
        mkdir -p "$(dirname "$pending")"
        : >"$pending"
        say "a job started while this update was running, so the app was not restarted and the job was left to finish."
        say "the new version is installed. Run this again when the job has finished, or with --force to restart now."
        return 0
    fi

    if restart_app; then
        state="now running"
    else
        state="installed"
    fi
    rm -f "$pending"
    "$bin" version | head -1 | sed "s/^/zoomies: $state: /"
}

main "$@"; exit $?

# The reverse proxy in front of the controller, when this deployment gets its
# certificate automatically.
#
# Zoomies terminates TLS itself when it is handed a certificate, so this exists
# for the one case it cannot cover: no certificate to hand, and no Cloudflare.
# Caddy asks Let's Encrypt for one, renews it, and redirects port 80 to 443 on
# its own -- which is the whole of what is needed and the reason the file is
# this short.
#
# It proxies to the controller on loopback, so the controller is never
# published to the internet itself.
{
	__ZOOMIES_ACME_GLOBAL__
}

__ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME__ {
	# X-Forwarded-For is set by Caddy, and the controller believes it because
	# the answer file names this proxy in trusted_proxies. Without that pair,
	# every audit row would record the proxy and the login rate limiter would
	# throttle the whole internet as one caller.
	reverse_proxy __ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR__:8080
}

# The marketplace deployment package

What a VPS provider needs to offer Zoomies as a one-click deployment, and what
an operator can run by hand to get the same result.

It deploys **a controller**. Zoomies is self-hosted and
bring-your-own-infrastructure: this puts the always-on half on one instance, and
the runner capacity stays yours. The default install also runs an agent on that
instance, so it can execute jobs from the first minute; set `ZOOMIES_MODE` to
`controller` when the runners live elsewhere.

## The files

| File | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `release.env` | The release this package installs: the controller image by tag and digest, the installer and its checksum, and the version a joining agent is given. Hand-edited when a new release becomes the baseline. |
| `images.lock` | Every image that release publishes, and the digest each tag resolved to. Generated by `make marketplace-lock`. |
| `inputs.env.example` | The settings that differ between one customer and the next. Copy it, fill it in. |
| `answers.yaml.tmpl` | The answers `zoomies init` is given, with the instance's own values still to substitute. |
| `bootstrap.sh` | First boot: install a container runtime, render the answers, run the pinned installer, wait for health, put a certificate holder in front if one is wanted, leave a note. |
| `Caddyfile.tmpl`, `proxy-compose.yml.tmpl` | The certificate holder, for `ZOOMIES_TLS=acme`. |
| `tunnel-compose.yml.tmpl` | The Cloudflare Tunnel daemon, for `ZOOMIES_TLS=tunnel`. |
| `cloud-init.yaml.tmpl` | The cloud-config the three files above are rendered into. |
| `render.sh` | Does the rendering. |

## Using it

```sh
cp inputs.env.example inputs.env
$EDITOR inputs.env                 # at minimum, the hostname
./render.sh inputs.env > cloud-init.yaml
```

Boot an Ubuntu 24.04 LTS instance with `cloud-init.yaml` as its user data. When
it comes up, `/etc/zoomies/first-login.txt` says how to finish: read the setup
token from the controller's log, create the first administrator in the browser,
connect GitHub, make a pool.

## What it will not do

**It carries no secret you have an alternative to.** Not the GitHub App's
private key, not the webhook secret, not an administrator password, not a join
token. A Cloudflare Tunnel token is the single exception, and it is optional:
leave it out and the instance still boots ready for you to paste it over SSH. Everything a provider's
form collects becomes instance metadata, which is readable by anything on the
instance that can reach the metadata service, kept in the provider's own
database, and printed in cloud-init's log, and a credential that has been
copied to all three places cannot be rotated out of them. `render.sh` refuses an
inputs file that sets one.

So the parts that need a credential happen afterwards, in the browser, over the
connection the operator already trusts. The first administrator is created with
the setup token the controller prints while no account exists; GitHub is
connected from the UI by an administrator who is already signed in.

**It offers no plain-HTTP public endpoint.** The origin often speaks HTTP
(that is what three of the five arrangements do) but something in front always
holds a certificate for the public name: a Cloudflare Tunnel dialling out from
this instance, Cloudflare in front of a published origin, a proxy here with a
certificate from Let's Encrypt, Zoomies itself with one you supply, or a load
balancer of yours. An unrecognised `ZOOMIES_TLS` is refused by name rather than
defaulted. [docs/marketplace.md](../../docs/marketplace.md) has all five, and
the table of which proxy each one believes.

**It has not been tested on a provider yet.** The implementation is complete and
its rendering is checked by tests in `internal/docs`; a pristine-VPS run, the
first-workflow journey and a pilot review are separate work and are not claimed
here.

# The answers `zoomies init` is given on this instance's first boot.
#
# Rendered by bootstrap.sh into /etc/zoomies/answers.yaml. Every key is one
# question the interactive installer would have asked, so this file is also the
# record of what setup decided -- worth reading before wondering why the
# controller came up the way it did.
#
# What is deliberately absent matters as much as what is here: no GitHub App
# credentials, no webhook secret and no administrator password. A containerised
# deployment creates its first administrator in the browser, and GitHub is
# connected there too, so nothing secret has to survive in instance metadata or
# on this disk to get from a booted image to a working fleet.

# single runs an agent inside the controller; controller runs none.
mode: __ZOOMIES_MODE__

# compose, because upgrading is then pulling one pinned image, and because the
# database lives in a volume the installer never opens -- which is what makes
# the browser-side administrator bootstrap the supported path.
deployment: compose
deployment_dir: /etc/zoomies
image: __ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE__
config_dir: /etc/zoomies

backend: docker

# For a containerised deployment this is the address the container is published
# on, not the listener: inside the container Zoomies always binds :8080, and
# what is chosen here is what the host exposes. Loopback means only this
# instance and whatever proxies from it can connect, which is what every
# arrangement except a certificate of your own wants.
bind: __ZOOMIES_BIND__

tls:
  # Quoted: an unquoted off is a boolean in YAML, not a word.
  #
  # "files" means Zoomies terminates TLS itself with the certificate below and
  # is published straight on 443. Anything else means something in front holds
  # the certificate -- the bundled proxy, or a load balancer of the provider's.
  mode: "__ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE__"
  # Empty unless the mode is files. The paths are the host's, and the
  # deployment mounts them into the container unchanged.
  cert_file: __ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE__
  key_file: __ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE__

trusted_proxies: [__ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES__]

# How GitHub and the browser reach this controller.
external_url: __ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL__

github:
  # Connected in the UI, by an administrator who is already signed in. The
  # unattended path would need an App's private key and webhook secret in this
  # file, which is exactly what a marketplace form must not collect.
  skip: true

#!/bin/sh
# First boot of a Zoomies instance deployed from a provider's marketplace.
#
# It is deliberately dull: install a container runtime, write an answer file,
# run the pinned installer, and leave a note saying how to finish. Everything
# that needs a secret -- the first administrator, the GitHub App -- happens
# afterwards in the browser, because a marketplace form's answers live in
# instance metadata and a boot log, and neither is a place for a credential.
#
# It is rendered into a cloud-config by render.sh and runs as root, once. A
# second run is safe: each step checks what is already there, so a boot that
# failed halfway can be resumed by running this again.
#
# Failure is loud and final. A half-built controller that answers on :8080 is
# worse than one that never started, because the first thing an operator does
# with a reachable Zoomies is point GitHub at it.
set -eu

# The paths are overridable so that the test suite can run the rendering half
# of this script against a temporary directory and check that a real boot would
# write an answer file `zoomies init` accepts. Proving that without a VM is
# worth a seam: the alternative is a test that reimplements the substitution
# below and then agrees with itself while the boot fails.
ENV_FILE=${ZOOMIES_ENV_FILE:-/etc/zoomies/marketplace.env}
ANSWERS_TMPL=${ZOOMIES_ANSWERS_TEMPLATE:-/etc/zoomies/answers.yaml.tmpl}
ANSWERS=${ZOOMIES_ANSWERS_FILE:-/etc/zoomies/answers.yaml}
CADDY_TMPL=${ZOOMIES_CADDY_TEMPLATE:-/etc/zoomies/Caddyfile.tmpl}
PROXY_TMPL=${ZOOMIES_PROXY_TEMPLATE:-/etc/zoomies/proxy-compose.yml.tmpl}
PROXY_DIR=${ZOOMIES_PROXY_DIR:-/etc/zoomies/proxy}
TUNNEL_TMPL=${ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_TEMPLATE:-/etc/zoomies/tunnel-compose.yml.tmpl}
TUNNEL_DIR=${ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_DIR:-/etc/zoomies/tunnel}
NOTES=${ZOOMIES_NOTES_FILE:-/etc/zoomies/first-login.txt}
LOG_TAG=zoomies-bootstrap

say() { echo "[$LOG_TAG] $*"; }
die() { echo "[$LOG_TAG] $*" >&2; exit 1; }

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the inputs

[ -r "$ENV_FILE" ] || die "$ENV_FILE is missing; the image was rendered without its inputs"
# shellcheck disable=SC1090
. "$ENV_FILE"

: "${ZOOMIES_RELEASE:?the rendered inputs name no release}"
: "${ZOOMIES_INSTALLER_URL:?the rendered inputs name no installer}"
: "${ZOOMIES_INSTALLER_SHA256:?the rendered inputs name no installer checksum}"
ZOOMIES_PROXY_IMAGE=${ZOOMIES_PROXY_IMAGE:-}
ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_IMAGE=${ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_IMAGE:-}
ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_TOKEN=${ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_TOKEN:-}

ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME=${ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME:-}
[ -n "$ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME" ] || die "no hostname was given: set ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME to the DNS name that points at this instance"

ZOOMIES_MODE=${ZOOMIES_MODE:-single}
case "$ZOOMIES_MODE" in
  single|controller) ;;
  *) die "mode $ZOOMIES_MODE is not one this package installs: use single or controller" ;;
esac

# Who holds the certificate for the public name. Refusing an unknown value by
# name beats publishing an origin to the internet in the clear because an input
# was spelled in a way nothing here reads.
#
# Three of the four leave the controller speaking plain HTTP, which is correct:
# the origin is not the public endpoint, and something in front of it is.
ZOOMIES_TLS=${ZOOMIES_TLS:-acme}
case "$ZOOMIES_TLS" in
  acme|files|tunnel|cloudflare|off) ;;
  *) die "TLS mode $ZOOMIES_TLS is not one this package installs: use acme, files, tunnel, cloudflare or off" ;;
esac

ZOOMIES_ACME_EMAIL=${ZOOMIES_ACME_EMAIL:-}
ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE=${ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE:-}
ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE=${ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE:-}
if [ "$ZOOMIES_TLS" = "files" ]; then
  if [ -z "$ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE" ] || [ -z "$ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE" ]; then
    die "TLS mode files needs ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE and ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE: the certificate this instance serves, and its key"
  fi
fi

# The listener, what the instance exposes, and which proxies it believes.
#
# The last of those is the one that goes wrong silently. X-Forwarded-For is
# read only from a peer in trusted_proxies, and CF-Connecting-IP only from a
# peer that is Cloudflare's own edge -- so the right answer differs between
# Cloudflare in front of a published origin and a tunnel, even though both are
# Cloudflare. Getting it wrong costs every audit row the real client's address
# and throttles the whole internet as one caller, and nothing reports it.
case "$ZOOMIES_TLS" in
  files)
    # The only arrangement where Zoomies itself is the public endpoint.
    ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR=${ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:-0.0.0.0}
    ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES=${ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES:-127.0.0.1/32,::1/128}
    ZOOMIES_BIND=0.0.0.0:443
    ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE=files
    # -k, because the question is whether the controller is answering, not
    # whether a certificate issued for the public name matches 127.0.0.1.
    HEALTH_URL=https://127.0.0.1/healthz
    HEALTH_CURL_OPTS=-k
    ;;
  cloudflare)
    # Cloudflare's edge connects to a published origin over plain HTTP on 80,
    # so the peer is Cloudflare and the word expands to its ranges -- which is
    # what makes CF-Connecting-IP, the one header a client cannot forge, count.
    ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR=${ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:-0.0.0.0}
    ZOOMIES_BIND=$ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:80
    ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE=off
    ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES=${ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES:-cloudflare}
    HEALTH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:80/healthz
    HEALTH_CURL_OPTS=
    ;;
  *)
    # acme, tunnel and off all reach the controller on loopback. For a tunnel
    # the peer is cloudflared on this machine rather than Cloudflare's edge, so
    # trusting Cloudflare's ranges would trust nothing that ever connects: the
    # address to believe is the local daemon's, and the header that survives is
    # X-Forwarded-For.
    ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR=${ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:-127.0.0.1}
    ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES=${ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES:-127.0.0.1/32,::1/128}
    ZOOMIES_BIND=$ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:8080
    ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE=off
    HEALTH_URL=http://$ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:8080/healthz
    HEALTH_CURL_OPTS=
    ;;
esac

ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL=${ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL:-https://$ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME}
ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR=${ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR:-/var/lib/zoomies}
ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE=${ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE:-}
[ -n "$ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE" ] || die "the rendered inputs name no controller image"

ZOOMIES_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP=${ZOOMIES_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP:-setup-token}
[ "$ZOOMIES_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP" = "setup-token" ] || \
  die "administrator bootstrap $ZOOMIES_ADMIN_BOOTSTRAP is not supported: setup-token is the only one that needs no secret in instance metadata"

say "deploying Zoomies $ZOOMIES_RELEASE for $ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL"

# ------------------------------------------------------------ the dependency

install_runtime() {
  if command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    say "a container runtime with compose is already here"
    return 0
  fi
  command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
    die "no container runtime, and this bootstrap only knows how to install one with apt: install Docker and compose, then run this again"

  say "installing the distribution's Docker and compose packages"
  export DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive
  # The distribution's own packages rather than a script piped from the
  # internet: this runs unattended on first boot, and a pipeline to a shell is
  # one more thing that can change between the day this was tested and the day
  # somebody deploys it.
  apt-get update -qq
  apt-get install -y -qq docker.io docker-compose-v2 ca-certificates curl
  systemctl enable --now docker
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ the data

prepare_data_dir() {
  # A compose deployment keeps the database in a named volume. Backing that
  # volume with a directory chosen here is what lets a provider's attached disk
  # hold it -- and what makes "where is my data" answerable without knowing how
  # Docker lays out its own storage.
  mkdir -p "$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR"
  # The published image runs as an unprivileged uid that does not exist on this
  # host. A directory owned by anyone else gives "unable to open database file
  # (14)" at the first start, which reads like corruption and is not.
  chown 65532:65532 "$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR"
  chmod 0750 "$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR"

  if docker volume inspect zoomies-data >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    say "the zoomies-data volume already exists; leaving it alone"
    return 0
  fi
  say "backing the zoomies-data volume with $ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR"
  docker volume create \
    --driver local \
    --opt type=none \
    --opt "device=$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR" \
    --opt o=bind \
    zoomies-data >/dev/null
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- the answers

render_answers() {
  [ -r "$ANSWERS_TMPL" ] || die "$ANSWERS_TMPL is missing; the image was rendered without its answer template"
  umask 077

  # Each CIDR is quoted on the way into the YAML flow sequence. An IPv6 one has
  # to be: ::1/128 unquoted starts a plain scalar with a colon, which is not a
  # scalar at all, and the parser stops on the whole answer file rather than on
  # the setting -- so the loopback default alone would have failed at boot.
  trusted=$(printf '%s' "$ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES" | awk -F, '{
    out = ""
    for (i = 1; i <= NF; i++) {
      gsub(/^[ \t]+|[ \t]+$/, "", $i)
      if ($i == "") continue
      out = out (out == "" ? "" : ", ") "\"" $i "\""
    }
    printf "%s", out
  }')

  sed \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_MODE__|$ZOOMIES_MODE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE__|$ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_IMAGE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_BIND__|$ZOOMIES_BIND|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE__|$ZOOMIES_TLS_MODE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE__|$ZOOMIES_TLS_CERT_FILE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE__|$ZOOMIES_TLS_KEY_FILE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_TRUSTED_PROXIES__|$trusted|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL__|$ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL|g" \
    "$ANSWERS_TMPL" > "$ANSWERS"

  # A placeholder nobody wired up would otherwise reach `zoomies init` as a
  # literal, and the failure would be a YAML value that looks like a mistake
  # rather than an omission.
  if grep -q '__ZOOMIES_[A-Z_]*__' "$ANSWERS"; then
    die "the answer file still has unfilled placeholders: $(grep -o '__ZOOMIES_[A-Z_]*__' "$ANSWERS" | sort -u | tr '\n' ' ')"
  fi
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------- the installer

run_installer() {
  script=$(mktemp)
  say "fetching the pinned installer"
  curl -fsSL --retry 3 --retry-delay 2 -o "$script" "$ZOOMIES_INSTALLER_URL"

  actual=$(sha256sum "$script" | cut -d' ' -f1)
  if [ "$actual" != "$ZOOMIES_INSTALLER_SHA256" ]; then
    rm -f "$script"
    die "the installer's checksum is $actual and this release pins $ZOOMIES_INSTALLER_SHA256; refusing to run it"
  fi

  say "installing Zoomies $ZOOMIES_RELEASE"
  sh "$script" --answers "$ANSWERS" --version "$ZOOMIES_RELEASE"
  rm -f "$script"
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- the proxy

render_proxy() {
  [ "$ZOOMIES_TLS" = "acme" ] || return 0
  if [ ! -r "$CADDY_TMPL" ] || [ ! -r "$PROXY_TMPL" ]; then
    die "the ACME path needs $CADDY_TMPL and $PROXY_TMPL, and the image was rendered without them"
  fi
  [ -n "$ZOOMIES_PROXY_IMAGE" ] || die "the rendered inputs name no proxy image, so the ACME path has nothing to run"

  say "writing the configuration for a certificate holder in front of the controller"
  mkdir -p "$PROXY_DIR" "$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR/caddy"

  # An empty email is not the same as no email: "email" alone is not a
  # directive, so the whole line goes rather than its value.
  acme_global=""
  [ -n "$ZOOMIES_ACME_EMAIL" ] && acme_global="email $ZOOMIES_ACME_EMAIL"

  sed \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_ACME_GLOBAL__|$acme_global|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME__|$ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR__|$ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR|g" \
    "$CADDY_TMPL" > "$PROXY_DIR/Caddyfile"

  sed \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_PROXY_IMAGE__|$ZOOMIES_PROXY_IMAGE|g" \
    -e "s|__ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR__|$ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR|g" \
    "$PROXY_TMPL" > "$PROXY_DIR/docker-compose.yml"
}

render_tunnel() {
  [ "$ZOOMIES_TLS" = "tunnel" ] || return 0
  [ -r "$TUNNEL_TMPL" ] || die "the tunnel path needs $TUNNEL_TMPL, and the image was rendered without it"
  [ -n "$ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_IMAGE" ] || die "the rendered inputs name no tunnel image, so the tunnel path has nothing to run"

  say "writing the tunnel daemon's configuration"
  mkdir -p "$TUNNEL_DIR"
  sed -e "s|__ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_IMAGE__|$ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_IMAGE|g" "$TUNNEL_TMPL" > "$TUNNEL_DIR/docker-compose.yml"

  # The token is written beside the compose file rather than into it, and only
  # if there is one. A deployment rendered without a token is the better shape:
  # the operator pastes it here over SSH and it never passes through instance
  # metadata, the provider's database or cloud-init's log.
  if [ -n "$ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_TOKEN" ]; then
    (umask 077; printf 'TUNNEL_TOKEN=%s\n' "$ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_TOKEN" > "$TUNNEL_DIR/.env")
  elif [ ! -f "$TUNNEL_DIR/.env" ]; then
    (umask 077; printf '# Paste the tunnel token from the Cloudflare dashboard, then:\n#   docker compose -f %s/docker-compose.yml up -d\nTUNNEL_TOKEN=\n' "$TUNNEL_DIR" > "$TUNNEL_DIR/.env")
  fi
}

start_tunnel() {
  [ "$ZOOMIES_TLS" = "tunnel" ] || return 0
  if ! grep -q '^TUNNEL_TOKEN=.' "$TUNNEL_DIR/.env" 2>/dev/null; then
    say "no tunnel token yet, so the tunnel is not started; $NOTES says where to paste one"
    return 0
  fi
  docker compose -f "$TUNNEL_DIR/docker-compose.yml" up -d
}

start_proxy() {
  [ "$ZOOMIES_TLS" = "acme" ] || return 0
  docker compose -f "$PROXY_DIR/docker-compose.yml" up -d

  if [ "${ZOOMIES_DNS:-pending}" != "ready" ]; then
    # Not a failure. Caddy retries, so an instance booted before its DNS record
    # existed becomes healthy on its own once the record does -- which is the
    # usual order when the provider assigns the address at boot.
    say "the certificate cannot be issued until $ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME resolves to this instance; the proxy will keep trying"
  fi
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- the notes

write_notes() {
  umask 022
  cat > "$NOTES" <<NOTE
Zoomies $ZOOMIES_RELEASE is installed on this instance.

  Address   $ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL
  Published $ZOOMIES_PUBLISH_ADDR:8080
  Data      $ZOOMIES_DATA_DIR (the zoomies-data volume)
  Answers   $ANSWERS

Finish setup in three steps.

1. Read this instance's setup token:

     docker compose -f /etc/zoomies/docker-compose.yml logs zoomies | grep 'setup token'

   It is printed only while no account exists, and a restart mints a new one.
   Holding it is the proof of ownership that an empty database is not: without
   it, whoever loads the page first would become the administrator.

2. Open $ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL, paste the token, and create the first
   administrator.

3. Connect GitHub from the UI. Nothing runs until a pool exists, so make one
   after that.
NOTE

  # What each arrangement still needs from a person, which is the part a
  # generic note would leave them to work out on their own.
  case "$ZOOMIES_TLS" in
    tunnel)
      cat >> "$NOTES" <<NOTE

This deployment publishes no port. Cloudflare serves HTTPS on
$ZOOMIES_HOSTNAME and a tunnel daemon on this instance dials out to it, so
there is no inbound rule, no DNS record of this machine's own and no
certificate here.
NOTE
      if grep -q '^TUNNEL_TOKEN=.' "$TUNNEL_DIR/.env" 2>/dev/null; then
        cat >> "$NOTES" <<NOTE
The tunnel is running with the token this instance was rendered with.
NOTE
      else
        cat >> "$NOTES" <<NOTE
The tunnel is not running yet, because it has no token. Create the tunnel in
the Cloudflare dashboard, point its public hostname at
http://127.0.0.1:8080, then:

  \$EDITOR $TUNNEL_DIR/.env          # paste the token
  docker compose -f $TUNNEL_DIR/docker-compose.yml up -d

Pasting it here rather than into the provider's form is deliberate: a token in
instance metadata is also in the provider's database and in cloud-init's log.
NOTE
      fi
      ;;
    cloudflare)
      cat >> "$NOTES" <<NOTE

This instance serves plain HTTP on port 80 for Cloudflare to proxy, and
believes X-Forwarded-For and CF-Connecting-IP from Cloudflare's own ranges.

Firewall port 80 to those ranges. Left open to everything, the origin is
reachable directly and Cloudflare is merely in front of it rather than in the
way -- so a caller who finds this address bypasses every rule set at the edge.
NOTE
      ;;
  esac
  chmod 0644 "$NOTES"

  if [ -d /etc/update-motd.d ]; then
    cat > /etc/update-motd.d/99-zoomies <<'MOTD'
#!/bin/sh
[ -r /etc/zoomies/first-login.txt ] && cat /etc/zoomies/first-login.txt
MOTD
    chmod 0755 /etc/update-motd.d/99-zoomies
  fi
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- the check

wait_for_health() {
  # The question is whether the controller answers, not whether compose
  # reported success: an image that starts and then exits on a bad setting
  # leaves a healthy-looking `up -d` behind it.
  i=0
  while [ "$i" -lt 60 ]; do
    # shellcheck disable=SC2086
    if curl -fsS $HEALTH_CURL_OPTS -o /dev/null "$HEALTH_URL"; then
      say "the controller is answering on $HEALTH_URL"
      return 0
    fi
    i=$((i + 1))
    sleep 2
  done
  die "the controller did not answer /healthz within two minutes; its log is: docker compose -f /etc/zoomies/docker-compose.yml logs zoomies"
}

# Rendering is everything this script decides; the rest is installing what it
# decided. Stopping here is how the tests read those decisions.
if [ "${ZOOMIES_RENDER_ONLY:-}" = "1" ]; then
  render_answers
  render_proxy
  render_tunnel
  say "rendered $ANSWERS and stopped, because ZOOMIES_RENDER_ONLY is set"
  exit 0
fi

install_runtime
prepare_data_dir
render_answers
run_installer
wait_for_health
render_proxy
start_proxy
render_tunnel
start_tunnel
write_notes

say "done. $NOTES says how to finish setup."

#cloud-config
# Zoomies, deployed from a provider's marketplace.
#
# This is a template. render.sh fills in the three blocks below from
# release.env and an inputs file, and what it prints is the user-data a
# provider boots. Rendering rather than templating in the provider's own
# console is the point: the rendered file is a fixed artefact that can be
# diffed, reviewed and archived beside the release it installs.
#
# Nothing secret belongs in here. Instance metadata is readable by anything on
# the instance that can reach the metadata service, it is kept in the
# provider's database, and it is printed in cloud-init's own log -- so the
# first administrator and the GitHub App are set up in the browser afterwards,
# and this file carries only settings.

write_files:
  # What the bootstrap was told, and what the release pins. Mode 0600 because
  # it is configuration for root, not because any of it is a credential.
  - path: /etc/zoomies/marketplace.env
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0600'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_ENV__

  # The answers `zoomies init` is given, with the instance's own values still
  # to be substituted at boot.
  - path: /etc/zoomies/answers.yaml.tmpl
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0600'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_ANSWERS_TMPL__

  # The certificate holder, used only when ZOOMIES_TLS is acme. Written either
  # way: an instance that is later moved onto its own certificate, or off one,
  # should not need a different image to do it.
  - path: /etc/zoomies/Caddyfile.tmpl
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_CADDYFILE__

  - path: /etc/zoomies/proxy-compose.yml.tmpl
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_PROXY_COMPOSE__

  # The tunnel daemon, used only when ZOOMIES_TLS is tunnel. Written either
  # way, for the same reason as the proxy above.
  - path: /etc/zoomies/tunnel-compose.yml.tmpl
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0644'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_TUNNEL_COMPOSE__

  - path: /usr/local/sbin/zoomies-bootstrap
    owner: root:root
    permissions: '0700'
    content: |
      __ZOOMIES_BOOTSTRAP__

runcmd:
  # One command, so that a failure is one exit status and cloud-init's own
  # status reports it. The script is idempotent: a boot that failed halfway can
  # be resumed by running it again over SSH.
  - [/usr/local/sbin/zoomies-bootstrap]

# A controller-only instance, answered in full: `zoomies init --answers
# controller-answers.yaml`.
#
# This is the shape a Terraform module or a configuration-management run
# writes: nobody is at the console, so every question the installer would ask
# is answered here, and nothing has to be read back out of a log afterwards.
# Replace the example values; the keys are the whole contract.
#
# It runs no agent. Runners live on the hosts that join it, each with
# `zoomies agent join` and a join token minted through the API by the account
# below -- so the settings page leaves out the agent settings this process has
# no use for.

# controller runs no embedded agent; the answer the file exists to give.
mode: controller

# native: a systemd service, and the installer creates the first account below
# on the console. A containerised controller creates it from the environment
# instead -- see ZOOMIES_BOOTSTRAP_* in docs/configuration.md.
deployment: native

# Zoomies terminates TLS itself with a certificate the provisioner put on disk,
# so the controller is reachable by agents on other hosts with nothing in front.
bind: 0.0.0.0:8443
tls:
  mode: files
  cert_file: /etc/zoomies/tls/fullchain.pem
  key_file: /etc/zoomies/tls/privkey.pem

# How agents, GitHub and the browser reach this controller.
external_url: https://zoomies.example.com:8443

# The first account, which holds the platform role. The password is read from
# a file the provisioner wrote with mode 0600 and is never written here.
# The installer records it in the audit log as auth.bootstrap, method
# answer_file.
admin:
  username: platform
  password_file: /etc/zoomies/bootstrap-password

github:
  # Connected later, in the UI or through the API, by the account above.
  skip: true

pool:
  # A controller with no agent has no runners of its own for a pool to
  # describe; pools are created once hosts have joined.
  skip: true

# Every image v1.3.0 deploys, and the digest its tag resolved to.
#
# Generated by `make marketplace-lock`; do not edit. Each line is one image
# reference and the digest it pointed at when this release was locked, so a
# deployment can be audited against what was published rather than against

# one: a controller resolves its runners from its own build tag, so pinning
# the controller pins every line below with it.
