# Explain, and enable, machine renting: design

**Status:** implemented (approach A), on draft pull request eyupio/zoomies#880.
**Date:** 11 October 2026.

## Goal

When a pool has work waiting and no machine is being rented for it, the operator
never has to guess why. The product says so in one plain sentence, in every
place somebody would wonder, with the one thing to change. An administrator can
fix the usual cause with one click and no restart. And a fleet like the reporter's
(four Linux Docker hosts and one Windows host, one Proxmox provider) rents a
machine for a full Linux pool without any extra configuration.

### Success criteria

1. In a fleet whose Linux Docker hosts are all full and which also holds a host
   that can never run the pool (a Windows host offering only `process`), a queued
   job for the Linux pool makes the machine planner buy a machine, up to the
   ceilings.
2. With renting switched off, or the fleet ceiling at zero, the Providers page,
   the provider's Pools tab, the pool page, the queued job's explanation and
   verdict, the problems drawer and the MCP `list_providers` tool all give the
   same sentence and the same fix. None of them says "would rent" without saying
   what stops it.
3. An administrator turns renting on from the Providers page in one click. It
   takes effect on the next machine pass, without a restart. Everyone else sees
   who to ask.
4. Nothing here spends money that was not asked for. `provider.enabled` still
   defaults to false and `provider.max_machines` still defaults to zero. The click
   is the explicit act, and it sets both.

## What was wrong

Two independent faults, found by reading the code and reproducing the second with
a model of the reporter's fleet (`scheduler.Decide` into `DecideMachines`, with
and without the Windows host).

**Renting was switched off, and nothing said so.** `provider.enabled` is off by
default and applied only at start (`internal/config/settings.go`), the machine
loop is only spawned when it is on (`internal/controller/controller.go`), and
every explanation path is silent while it is off:

- `provisioningHeld` builds the "held" sentence a provider card and the MCP tool
  present as "why no machine may be bought right now". It never consults the
  setting, so `held` was empty.
- `machineProblems` and the configuration validator return before raising
  anything while the setting is off, by design.
- `GET /meta` carries `providers_available`, but nothing in `web/src` reads it.
- The Pools tab's "Would rent" answers only the two selectors and the machine's
  shape. It says nothing about whether renting is on.
- `DecideMachines` already computes why a machine is not bought (a ceiling, no
  provider serving the pool), but the pass only logs it, and the ceiling
  sentences are not even logged.

**A host that can never run the pool stopped the fleet being called full.**
`hostSet.why` set `atCapacity` to `full + throttled + committed == len(hs.hosts)`,
counting hosts that can never run the pool (wrong backend, platform, selector or
size) in the denominator. `DecideMachines` buys only for a pool whose plan is
`BlockedAtCapacity` or `BlockedNoEligibleHost`, so one Windows host beside a Linux
fleet meant a Linux pool was never reported full and a machine was never bought.
History shows this was a side effect, not a decision: the `len(hs.hosts)`
denominator was written on 4 September, before any machine planner existed, and the
two test rows that pin the mixed case justify only the other flag
(`noEligibleHost`).

## Decisions

- **Consent model (A).** Renting stays opt-in. An administrator turns it on with
  one click that sets `provider.enabled` and `provider.max_machines` together.
  Rejected: turning it on when a provider is added (B), which spends money without
  a second confirmation and reverses the documented default; and explanations
  only (C), which leaves a hidden setting and a restart in the way.
- **Hosts that could run the pool but are cordoned, silent or incompatible keep
  blocking a purchase, as today.** A blip must not buy a machine, and there is no
  grace period on the buy side. Ignoring them is a separate decision that needs a
  grace period; it is a listed follow-up.
- **The fleet ceiling is shown to viewers.** The per-provider ceilings already are
  on `GET /providers`; the fleet figure is the same order of sensitivity.
- **Turning renting off still stops the whole loop**, deletes and ownership checks
  included, exactly as before. `provider.paused` is the gentle switch and the
  setting's text says so. A warning problem is raised when renting is off while
  machines are still owned, because nothing is then tending them.

## Design

### 1. At capacity means every host that could run the pool

In `hostSet.why` (`internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`), count how many hosts pass
`HostCouldRun` (the configured-compatible test, with the weather left out) and how
many of those are out of slots (full, throttled or committed, as the ladder already
classifies them). Then:

```go
atCapacity := full+throttled+committed == len(hs.hosts) ||
    (candidates > 0 && waiting == candidates)
```

The first disjunct is today's rule and is kept so that nothing that was reported
full stops being reported full (a too-small host the ladder called throttled before
it asked whether the pool fits at all is still out of slots). The second admits the
mixed fleet. `onlyFull`, which chooses the fix text, takes the same shape over
full and throttled hosts only, so a mixed fleet gets "wait for a job to finish,
raise a host's capacity, or add a host" rather than the generic fallback.
`noEligibleHost` is unchanged. Held and warming hosts that could run the pool still
count as candidates that are not out of slots, so a pressure hold never buys a
machine.

Visible effects: `pool.no_capacity` for a merely full mixed fleet becomes a warning
("waiting for a host with room") instead of an error ("nowhere to run them"); the
capacity-demand webhook fires for such a fleet; usage records count its minutes at
capacity.

### 2. The planner returns a verdict for each pool with unmet demand

`DecideMachines` (`internal/controller/machinedemand.go`) gains `MachinePlan.Pools
[]PoolRenting`. Its decisions do not change. A verdict is recorded at each point it
already branches, for every pool the scheduler reports blocked whose `Desired`
exceeds its `Current`. A pool the scheduler can place itself, or whose shortfall is
covered by free slots on hosts that can run it, gets no verdict:

| State | When | Setting to change |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `renting` | this pass reserves a machine that covers it (possibly only part of it) | none |
| `on_its_way` | machines already being built cover it | none |
| `waiting` | the scheduler is not blocked in a way a machine fixes: a candidate host is held, starting runners, cordoned, silent or incompatible | none |
| `ceiling` | a limit stops the machine it needs | `provider.max_machines` for the fleet limit, none for a provider's own |
| `unserved` | no provider may rent for it (a selector says no) or none builds a machine that suits it | none |

Two more states are overlaid by the controller, because the planner is pure and
does not know them: `held` (the provider could, and `provisioningHeld` says it may
not) and `off` (renting is switched off; every verdict that would have been
`renting` or `ceiling` becomes `off` and says how many machines it would rent).

A verdict carries `state`, a one-sentence `summary`, a `fix`, the `setting` when
one setting changes it, the provider, `queued`, `short`, `machines` and `since`
(when the oldest machine on its way was asked for). Sentences never contain a
running clock or a counter that moves while the fleet stays as it is, because
anything that reaches the problems list is re-sent whenever its JSON differs. Counts
of jobs, slots and machines are fine: they move only when the fleet does, as the
queue count in the `pool.no_capacity` title already does. Times travel as `since`.

### 3. The loop keeps the verdict, and renting applies live

- `provider.enabled` becomes live (`Live: true`, no `RestartReason`). The machine
  loop is always spawned, as the kennel loop is, and `ReconcileMachines` still does
  nothing while renting is off: no recovery, sweep, drain, delete or create.
- While renting is off, or this controller may not act, the pass still reads the
  snapshot, runs `DecideMachines`, and stores the result. This is the rule
  `Controller.apply` already follows for a fenced fleet: decide and publish, but do
  not act, so an operator can tell "nothing to do" from "not allowed to".
- The stored report is replaced under its own lock, never `machines.mu`, which is
  held for a whole pass. The report is as old as the last pass, at most one
  `provider.interval`, and a settings change or a provider change wakes the loop.
- `provisioningHeld` gains a clause for the switch, after the recovery fence, so
  `ProviderView.Held` and `zoomies providers list` stop saying a provider is fine
  when nothing can be bought.
- When a pass finds that a provider's held sentence has changed (renting
  switched on or off, for example) it republishes that provider's view
  (`provider.updated`), so open pages move without a reload. A settings change
  already wakes the loop at once, so this follows the click within a second.

### 4. One verdict, every surface

**Route.** `GET /api/v1/providers/renting` (a viewer's, action `providers.read`):

```json
{
  "state": "off",
  "summary": "Renting is switched off: this controller is not allowed to rent machines, so work with nowhere to run waits for the hosts it has.",
  "fix": "Turn on Rent machines in Settings and set Machines the fleet may rent.",
  "setting": "provider.enabled",
  "enabled": false, "paused": false, "max_machines": 0,
  "suggested_max_machines": 2, "owned": 0,
  "decided_at": "2026-10-11T13:12:00Z",
  "pools": [
    { "pool_id": "pool_example", "pool_name": "zoomies-linux-x64", "state": "off",
      "summary": "Would rent 1 machine for this pool, but renting is switched off.",
      "fix": "Turn on renting.", "setting": "provider.enabled",
      "provider_id": "prv_example", "provider_name": "proxmox-lab",
      "queued": 1, "short": 1, "machines": 0 }
  ]
}
```

The fleet `state` is `none` (no enabled provider other than demo fixtures), `off`,
`no_ceiling` (renting is on and the fleet ceiling is zero) or `on`.
`suggested_max_machines` is the sum of the enabled providers' own ceilings, at
least one: what the click sets. `pools` is empty before the first pass.

**Held.** `ProviderView.Held` says renting is off (section 3).

**Problem `provider.renting_off`.** Raised wherever an enabled non-demo provider
exists and renting is off, from a function that runs even though `machineProblems`
returns early while renting is off.
Severity is chosen in code: a warning when a pool's verdict is `off` or machines
are still owned, otherwise info. The setting is `provider.enabled`. Fleet audience,
a public-status sentence ("Machines are not being rented, so jobs wait for the
machines the fleet already has."), a row in `docs/problem-codes.md`, and a
regenerated catalogue.

**Pool, job and verdict text.** `pool.no_capacity` gains the pool's verdict summary
in its detail and puts the verdict's fix first. The queued-job explanation
(`explain.go`) and the job verdict (`why.go`) do the same, the latter as an
evidence line labelled "renting" and a next step linking to `/providers`.

**MCP.** `list_providers` splices in `renting` from the new route, best effort, as
it already does for `providers_available`. A single call then answers the original
question. The words the description tests pin stay.

### 5. The Providers page

- `getProviderRenting()` in the API client. Providers and provider-detail load it
  with their other data and reload on `provider.updated`, `machine.updated` and
  `problems.updated`.
- A new `RentingNotice` shows above the metrics for `off` and `no_ceiling`. For an
  administrator it carries **Turn on renting** (or **Allow N machines**) and a
  ceiling field defaulting to `suggested_max_machines`; one `PATCH /settings` sets
  `provider.enabled` and `provider.max_machines` together. Everyone else sees the
  sentence and who can change it. An environment-pinned setting shows the server's
  own refusal. For `on` it shows nothing: a machine being built is told on the Pools tab
and the pool page, and a notice that is always there stops being read.
- The Pools tab shows each pool's live verdict under "Would rent" and keeps the
  static reason for "Would not rent".
- Tokens only: the notice is a pure explanation (`--z-accent-subtle` and
  `--z-accent-border`), danger only for failure. No new library. Logic lives in
  `lib/providers/renting.ts` so it is unit-testable.

The notice, for tone:

> **Renting is switched off.** proxmox-lab passed its check, but this
> controller is not allowed to rent machines yet, so work with nowhere to run will
> wait. Right now zoomies-linux-x64 has 1 job waiting and every host that can run
> it is full: with renting on, 1 machine would be built for it straight away.
> [Turn on renting] up to [2] machines at once. You can pause or lower this at any
> time.

## Docs and generated files

# Eli PR delay: first calculation slice

Status: implementation started at the owner's request, 12 October 2026.
Package ZF-242; enhancement handoff track E1. Local baseline `1e745d25`;
upstream refreshed to `d382fb7a` before publication. Neither inspected tree has
`internal/analysis` yet. Reconcile with any ZF-241
implementation before integrating; do not replace another analysis package.

## Scope and contracts

This slice implements the pure calculation and behavioural fixtures. It does
not expose a route, MCP tool or UI action, and makes no GitHub or model request.
No source, mutation or dispatch permission changes.

`analysis.MergeDelay` takes a snapshot with a pinned head, independently observed
current head, target branch, observation window, explicit protection/observation
coverage, opaque required-check IDs and observations mapped by a future reader.
The reader is responsible for producer identity and rules applying to that
target branch. It must not derive required checks from job names or silently
reuse default-branch rules. Separate matrix checks can have separate required IDs;
multiple matrix instances mapped to one identity remain ambiguous.

Observations identify their run, logical instance and attempt. The highest
attempt within an instance supersedes earlier observations; independent runs or
instances claiming the same required identity are ambiguous. Other heads cannot
contribute to the pinned head's timing. Absent current-head evidence is unknown;
a different current head supersedes the snapshot.

Result version `merge-delay-v1` records per-check states and known timing, plus
the last observed completed required check. It never claims a dependency critical
path, cause of slowness, safe optimisation or complete merge readiness. The result
has at most 500 required checks and the input at most 5,000 observations. Oversize
inputs are refused rather than silently truncated.

Pre-start wait covers queue-to-job-start. When runner provisioning start is
known, split that interval into queue-to-provisioning and provisioning-to-start.
Do not sum pre-start wait and startup again. Missing provisioning time leaves
queue/startup unknown while retaining known pre-start and execution intervals.
Malformed, reversed or future timestamps produce invalid timing, not zero wait.
All completion delays are relative to the explicit head observation window.

Complete observations and protection may produce checks-passed, checks-failed
or checks-pending. Missing, unmapped, ambiguous or invalid evidence yields
incomplete. No required checks yields its own state. These describe check
observations only; approvals, conflicts and merge queues are outside the contract.

## Evidence and remaining integration

Behavioural fixtures cover interval accounting, partial/refused reads, external
checks, pending/failing checks, old heads, unknown currentness, retries, matrix
members, competing producers, absent timestamps, stable ordering, input bounds
and no-required-check semantics. The purity test forbids IO imports and implicit
clock reads in production code.

## Joining evidence

Only checks posted by GitHub Actions can map to the protection reader's
Actions-pinned requirements. A check's canonical run/job-link hint must match
a retained job's run ID, job ID, repository, installation, head and exact check
name. Unknown attempts, duplicate job records or unverified links remain
incomplete. A result never borrows a passing job from another installation or
revision. Names used for matching are replaced by opaque per-snapshot IDs.

Unpinned/external requirements remain counted as unmapped checks. Missing
protection, partial job collections and malformed or inconsistent outcomes
cannot become an all-clear. Closed PRs and changed target branches are refused;
changed heads and unavailable final currentness retain the core's explicit
states. No record is read without the future caller's authorisation checks.

## Timing

Queue/provisioning/execution intervals come from job evidence, with unknown
phases left absent. An optional `CheckCompletedAt` in the core separates the
required check's reporting completion from the job's execution completion.
Reporting time contributes to observed completion delay, not execution time.
Reversed or future reporting timestamps are invalid rather than normalised.

No commit/push time is invented. The caller must define the observation window
honestly; starting at an observed queued job is not a measurement of the full
time since the developer pushed. No dependency critical path or complete merge
readiness is inferred.

output, external requirements, missing coverage, racing outcomes, known startup,
reporting delay, retargeted/closed/stale PRs and bounds. Package vet, full
repository tests and formatting are run before final publication; record any
failure as such. No real-provider evaluation or performance benchmark is claimed.

contract. Freeze repository selection, source freshness, request budgets and
coverage before adding MCP/CLI or UI. Do not let a transport accept arbitrary

# Eli repair history Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Recent repairs gets server-side paging and filters, row selection with a frozen select-all, and a bulk **Clear from history** that hides rows without deleting them.

**Architecture:** A nullable `cleared_at` on `eli_repairs` hides a row from the history while the budget, deduplication, own-commit and allowance readers keep seeing it. The store gains a paged and filtered list, a clearable-id selection and a per-id clear. The API serves them as `GET /assistant/repairs` (now filtered and paged), `GET /assistant/repairs/selection` and `POST /assistant/repairs/bulk`. The history card moves out of `EliRepairs.svelte` into its own component.

**Tech Stack:** Go and SQLite (`internal/store`, `internal/api`), OpenAPI with generated clients, Svelte 5 runes, Playwright against the built binary.

**Spec:** `roadmap/plans/2026-10-12-eli-repair-history.md` (approved, including the migration).

## Two departures from the spec

1. **No demo-seed rows.** The spec said `internal/controller/seed.go` would gain about sixty repairs. The repo keeps repair history out of `SeedDemo` on purpose: only the screenshot harness adds two sample rows, through `web/tests/support/repair-fixture`, while its controller is stopped. Sixty seeded rows would also turn the docs' "sample history: a passed repair and an attempt needing attention" screenshots false. The browser tests therefore mock the three endpoints with `page.route`, as the Eli chat specs already do, and the real filtering, paging, scoping and clear rules are proven by Go tests against a real store and the real handlers.
2. **`ListEliRepairs` has 16 test call sites** in three packages. Replacing it, as the spec says, means a mechanical edit of each (Task 1).

## Global Constraints

* Migration `internal/store/migrations/0100_eli_repair_cleared.sql`: nullable `cleared_at INTEGER` (epoch milliseconds), no index. It is not added to `eliRepairCols`.
* **Clearing hides a row and nothing else.** `EnqueueEliRepair`'s budget and deduplication, `IsEliRepairCommit`, `EliRepairBudget`, `NextEliRepair` and `CheckingEliRepairs` never read `cleared_at`.
* Only `internal/store` writes SQL; `internal/api` is transport.
* State groups, defined once in the store: **active** `queued`, `working`, `checking`; **passed** `succeeded`; **attention** every other state. Trigger `automatic` means `trigger = 'automatic'`; `requested` means anything else.
* Paging uses the house `Limit` and `Offset` parameters: default 50, maximum 500. Selection returns at most 500 ids. A bulk request carries 1 to 500 ids and the single action `clear`.
* A bad `group`, `trigger`, `action` or `ids`, or a `repo` over 200 characters, is a 422 with a field error.
* Per-id clear errors are exactly `not found` and `still running`.
* Scope: administrators (`ActionAssistantRead`) reach every row; everyone else only rows whose `user_id` is theirs and not empty. *Amended by the final review:* that is the rule for the list and the selection, which are reads. The bulk clear is a write, so its wide reach uses `ActionAssistantWrite`: an administrator's token narrowed to `assistant:own` passes `ActionAssistantRead` and must not be able to clear everyone's repairs. `eliRepairScope` in `internal/api/handlers_eli_repairs.go` is the one place the rule is written.
* Audit: `assistant.repair_clear`, target kind `eli_repair`, detail holds the count and the ids, never repair text.
* Voice: British spelling, no em dashes, no `--`, comments say why. Test names are sentences.
* Commit messages are imperative sentences in sentence case with no prefix, ending with the two trailer lines the session was given (`Co-Authored-By` and `Claude-Session`).
* UI: tokens only, existing `Pagination`, `Checkbox`, `ConfirmDialog`, `Field`, `Select`, `Input` and `Button`, no new library, every control labelled.
* Before each push (steward skill): `make build-nogui`, `make fmt` then `make lint`, tests for what changed, generated files regenerated and not edited. Before the last push, the whole suite.

## Review Focus

1. A person who guesses another person's repair id in a clear gets `not found`, the same as for an id that does not exist, and the row is untouched. (Task 1, Task 2)
2. A repository search of `%`, `_` or `\` is literal text, and one of only spaces means no filter. (Task 1)
3. A person who asks again for a pull request whose repair they cleared sees that row back in their history. (Task 1)
4. A clear that empties the page being viewed, or leaves the offset past the new total, steps back instead of showing an empty page. (Task 3 unit, Task 4 browser)
5. A selection survives the ten-second refresh and page changes, is dropped by a filter change, and never holds an in-flight row. (Task 4)

## Threat and failure-mode review

`CONTRIBUTING.md` asks for this on authorisation and deletion paths.

* **Reaching another person's rows by id:** every id is checked against the caller's scope inside the same transaction as the write, and a foreign id and a missing id answer alike. Task 1 and Task 2 test it.
* **A viewer clearing history they do not own, or clearing everything:** non-administrators are scoped to their own rows. An administrator clearing everything is the point of the feature, behind a confirmation that says what it does.
* **Using a clear to get round the spend cap or to re-run a webhook:** impossible by construction, since every guard keeps reading cleared rows. Task 1 pins each one.
* **Clearing a row that is still running:** refused as `still running`. Finished states are terminal, so a row that passes the check cannot become active again before the write; both happen in one writer transaction.
* **A mass clear by mistake:** the rows are kept, so it is recoverable by an operator in the database, but the UI has no restore. The dialog says so, and restoring is out of scope.
* **Evidence:** one audit row per request with the ids cleared.

# Page, filter and clear Eli's repair history

Draft for review, 12 October 2026, written against checkout `e104846`. Nothing
here is built yet. The design below was agreed in conversation: the owner chose
**Clear from history** over a hard delete, approved server-side paging and
filters, a frozen select-all snapshot and a bulk clear, and asked for this spec
before any plan or code.

## What was asked

**Recent repairs** (the card on the Eli repairs page and on Settings, Eli AI
Assistant, which are one component) needs paging, filtering and a bulk delete
with a select-all.

## What the code does today

| Fact | Where | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| History is one unpaged call, newest 100 rows | `listEliRepairs` in `internal/store/queries_eli_repairs.go` (`LIMIT 100`) | Anything older is unreachable, and there is no total |
| The four-way "Show" filter runs in the browser over those 100 rows | `visibleRepairs` in `web/src/lib/settings/EliRepairs.svelte` | A filter cannot find a repair outside the newest 100 |
| The same three state lists are written out in three places | Same component | A new state has to be added in each |
| No route removes a repair | `internal/api/router.go` | Nothing to build a delete on |
| Visibility is decided in the handler: administrators see every row, everyone else their own rows | `handleEliRepairs` | Scoping for a bulk action must match it exactly |

## Why clearing is not deleting

A repair row is history, and it is also the ledger several safety rules read.
Removing one would weaken all of them, and the person pressing "delete all"
would not know.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  row["eli_repairs row"] --> list["History list and selection"]
  row --> budget["Daily budget: rows in the last 24 hours, per repository and per person"]
  row --> dedup["Deduplication: webhook delivery keys are permanent"]
  row --> guard["Own-commit guard: Eli does not repair its own repair commit"]
  row --> offers["Offer eligibility, which counts the same rows"]
  cleared["cleared_at set"] -. "hides the row from" .-> list
```

| Reader | Where | If the row were deleted |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Daily budget | `EnqueueEliRepair` (`internal/store/queries_eli_repairs.go`) | The limit resets, so clearing becomes a way round the spend cap |
| Deduplication | `dedup_key` unique constraint, same function | A redelivered webhook runs a second repair |
| Own-commit guard | `IsEliRepairCommit`, used at `internal/controller/eli_repairs.go:135` and `internal/controller/eli_experience.go:232` | An automatic repair loop becomes possible |
| Offer eligibility | `internal/store/queries_eli_opportunities.go:57` | Offers ignore attempts already spent |

So **clearing hides a row from the history and nothing else.** A row gains a
`cleared_at` timestamp; every reader above keeps seeing it. The button says
"Clear from history", not "Delete", because the row is kept and the dialog says
what that means.

## Design

### Data

Migration `0100_eli_repair_cleared.sql` adds a nullable `cleared_at INTEGER`
(epoch milliseconds, like the table's other timestamps) to `eli_repairs`. It is
not added to `eliRepairCols`: the column is read only by the history queries and
written only by the clear, so the insert and the scan stay as they are. No index
yet; the guards already scan this table by repository and time without one, and
that is the point to revisit if it grows.

### Store (`internal/store`)

* `ListEliRepairsPage(ctx, EliRepairFilter)` replaces `ListEliRepairs` and
  `ListEliRepairsForOwner`. The filter carries the owner scope (all, or one
  person), a state group, a repository substring, a trigger, a limit and an
  offset. It returns the page and the total of matching, uncleared rows. Order is
  newest first with the id as tie-break, so paging is stable.
* The state groups are defined once, in the store: **active** is `queued`,
  `working` and `checking`; **passed** is `succeeded`; **attention** is every
  other state (`checks_failed`, `interrupted`, `unverified`, `superseded`,
  `blocked`, `failed`). The Svelte component stops repeating them.
* The repository filter is a case-insensitive substring with `%`, `_` and `\`
  escaped. Trigger is `automatic` or `requested`; the stored `mention` value is
  what `requested` means.
* `EliRepairIDs(ctx, EliRepairFilter, cap)` returns the ids a select-all would
  take: matching, uncleared and **clearable** (not active), plus the total.
* `ClearEliRepairs(ctx, ids, scope)` runs in the single writer transaction and
  answers per unique id, in the order asked:
  * an id that does not exist, or that the caller may not see, is `not found`
    (the same answer for both, so ids cannot be probed);
  * an active row is `still running`;
  * an already cleared row is `ok`, so a repeat is harmless;
  * anything else is cleared.
* **No guard changes.** The budget count, the dedup lookup, `IsEliRepairCommit`,
  the offer query, `NextEliRepair` and `CheckingEliRepairs` never read
  `cleared_at`.
* One deliberate reader of it: when `EnqueueEliRepair` answers a new request or
  offer with an *existing* row (the in-flight and "already succeeded" cases), it
  clears that row's `cleared_at`, so the person sees the outcome of what they
  just asked for instead of an empty list. A retry of a failed `ui:` request
  already inserts a new row and needs nothing.

### API (`api/openapi.yaml`, `internal/api`)

| Route | Change | Role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET /assistant/repairs` | Gains `group` (`attention`, `active`, `passed`), `repo`, `trigger` (`automatic`, `requested`), `limit` and `offset` (the house `Limit` and `Offset` parameters). Returns `{items, total}`. An unknown `group` or `trigger` is a 422 with a field error, because a filter that silently widens would show the wrong history. | viewer, as now |
| `GET /assistant/repairs/selection` | New. The same filters, no paging. Returns `{ids, total, truncated}`: the clearable matches, at most 500, frozen at the moment of the call so rows arriving later are not swept in. Past 500 the page says so. | viewer |
| `POST /assistant/repairs/bulk` | New. `{action: clear, ids}` with 1 to 500 ids and one action for now. Returns `{results: [{id, ok, error?}]}` like `/machines/bulk`. | viewer |

Scoping for all three is the existing rule: administrators reach every row,
everyone else only rows whose `user_id` is theirs and not empty. A clear is
written to the audit log as `assistant.repair_clear` with the count and the ids,
never the repair's text.

The default page is 50, the house default, where the call used to return up to
100. Only the UI calls it today. `EliRepairList` gains a required `total`.

Everything that has to move together: `api/openapi.yaml`, the regenerated
`internal/api/openapi_spec.go` and `web/src/lib/api/schema.d.ts`,
`web/src/lib/api/client.ts`, `docs/api-surface.md`, `router.go`, and the
route and role table in `internal/api/api_test.go`.

### UI

Recent repairs moves out of the 650-line `EliRepairs.svelte` into
`web/src/lib/repairs/RepairHistory.svelte`. The parent keeps the cards and the
setup, passes down a callback for "Review another attempt", and its `reload()`
(the page header's Refresh) calls the history's own.

* **Filters:** the state group (the four labels used today), a repository search
  (debounced), and trigger (any, automatic, requested). A change resets the
  page and the selection.
* **Paging:** the existing `Pagination` component, with its page sizes taken from
  the preferences the other lists use. After a clear that empties the page, step
  back one.
* **Selection:** a checkbox per row and a header checkbox for the rows shown
  (indeterminate when some are chosen). Once every shown row is chosen and more
  match, **Select all N matching** reads the selection endpoint and chooses those
  ids; past 500 it says "500 of N selected". One set of chosen ids serves both,
  and it survives the 10-second poll and moving between pages.
* **In-flight rows** have a disabled checkbox with a title saying why.
* **Clearing:** a bar above the list says how many are chosen and offers **Clear
  from history** and **Clear selection**. The confirmation says what the button
  does: the rows stop showing here, still count towards the daily limit, and Eli
  will not repair its own commits again. The outcome is reported as the Queue
  page does: how many were cleared and, in a disclosure, which were skipped and
  why.
* **Empty states:** "No repairs match these filters", with **Clear filters**,
  is separate from "No repairs yet".
* House rules: `Pagination`, `Checkbox` and `ConfirmDialog` as they are, tokens
  only, no new library, labels on every control, an `aria-live` selection bar,
  and a layout that wraps on a phone without sideways scrolling.

## Tests

**Go**

* Store: the filters and the total; paging is stable across pages and with equal
  timestamps; owner scoping; `%` and `_` in a search are literal; the clear rules
  (`not found` for someone else's id, `still running`, idempotent repeat); and
  one test per guard proving it still counts a cleared row (budget, dedup,
  `IsEliRepairCommit`, offers). A request that dedups onto a cleared row brings it
  back.
* API: the three routes in the role table, an owner cannot clear another
  person's row, a 422 for a bad `group`, `trigger`, action or an empty or
  oversized id list, per-id results in the order asked, and the audit row.
* The demo seed (`internal/controller/seed.go`) gains about sixty finished
  repairs spread over states, repositories, triggers and dates, so the pages and
  the browser tests have rows. They are finished only: a queued or checking row
  would be picked up by the repair worker in a controller that has no GitHub
  behind it. `seed_test.go` and `seed_demo_isolation_test.go` keep their
  promises.

**Playwright** (`web/tests/repairs.spec.ts`, desktop and mobile)

* Filtering and paging reach rows beyond the first hundred, and the count is the
  server's.
* Select the rows shown, then select all matching; clear; the list, the total and
  the page update, and the dialog's wording is the true one.
* A selection survives the poll and a page change; a filter change drops it.
* An in-flight row has a disabled checkbox. The seed has none, so this test
  injects one into the list response; the rule itself is held by the Go tests.

**Unit** (`web/unit`): the state group and trigger mapping, and the selection
helper if one is split out.

**Docs:** `docs/eli.md` (a short paragraph on the history and on what Clear does
and does not do) and `docs/api-surface.md` (the changed row and the two new
ones). Prose follows the repository voice: British spelling, no em dashes.

## Delivery

Commits on `claude/brave-ramanujan-jkd9iw`, one draft pull request. The first
(already made) is the Eli message-size handling, which touches different files.
The second is this spec. The third is the change itself, built test first: the Go
store and API tests, then the migration and handlers, then the component and its
browser tests.

## Out of scope

* Restoring a cleared row.
* Hard deletion and retention. Rows are kept for good, as they are now.
* Sorting, and searching by pull request number.
* Exposing the history through the MCP server or the CLI.

## Points for the reviewer

1. **A new request surfaces a cleared row.** Chosen so the outcome of what a
   person just asked for is never hidden by an earlier clear. The alternative,
   leaving it hidden, is simpler and worse.
2. **The selection cap is 500**, the bulk limit, and the page says when it bites.
   The Queue page's 5,000 is for a table that grows much faster.
3. **The default page of 50** replaces an unpaged 100.

# A live public demo, and the public view it needs: design **Status:** approved approach; the public view is built on this branch, and the demo is hosted on InstaPods. **Date:** 12 October 2026. ## Goal The landing page's "Try the demo" button takes a person to a real fleet they can look around without installing anything, signing in or owning a GitHub App. The fleet is live: jobs queue, runners start, logs stream and runners are destroyed while the visitor watches. Nothing a visitor does can change the fleet, read anything about the people who run it, or cost anyone money. Today the button leads to the quickstart's "Just looking?" section, which asks for a terminal and a download and then shows a fixture fleet that never moves. That demo stays, because it is the one that needs no network and shows Eli, but it is no longer the first thing a visitor is asked to do. ### Success criteria 1. A visitor opening `https://demo.zoomies.sh` lands on the Overview of a live fleet with no sign-in form, sees a line saying this is a read-only public view, and can open any pool, runner, job, host or log. 2. Every change the API offers answers a visitor with 403 and a sentence saying the public view is read-only, whether it is asked for through the UI, the REST API or MCP. 3. A visitor never reads the audit log, accounts, tokens, settings, sessions, MCP connections, AI context or any assistant conversation, through any of those three, including the live event stream. 4. Anyone can connect their own assistant to `https://demo.zoomies.sh/mcp` with no credential and ask about the fleet with the read-only tools. 5. Whoever runs the demo signs in as usual and gets their own role back. 6. The setting is off by default, and a controller with it on says so in its problems list, as every setting that weakens the default posture does. ## Decisions Taken with the owner on 12 October 2026, one question at a time. | Question | Decision | | --- | --- | | What the demo is | **A live fleet**, not the fixture hosted. Visitors watch real jobs. | | How visitors get in | **No sign-in.** A new public view: an anonymous request is a visitor. | | What it runs | **A public demo organisation's scheduled workflows**, not this repository's CI, so a stranger's pull request never runs on it. | | Where it lives | **InstaPods, two pods** (revised the same day from one VM). A web pod runs the controller with the public view; a worker pod with no public address runs `zoomies agent` on the process backend, because pods offer no Docker. Jobs never share a pod with the database or the GitHub App key. | | How a pod gets Zoomies | **A published release, downloaded and checked against its checksums** by the pod's build command, not compiled there: the Go preset has neither Go 1.27 nor Node for the UI. `dev` until the public view ships in a release. | | Eli and MCP | **MCP read-only for anyone. Eli stays out of the public view.** Chatting is an administrator's action and spends a model provider's money; the local demo's fixture provider remains the way to try Eli without a key. | | What this branch does | **The design, then the public view in the product, with its docs.** The VM, the organisation and DNS are the owner's, from the runbook below. | ## Design ### 1. The setting `security.public_view`, a boolean, off by default, `ZOOMIES_PUBLIC_VIEW` as its override, platform scope, applied at restart for the reason `security.disable_auth` is (the authentication service takes its security settings when it is built). With it on, the configuration validator raises `auth.public_view`, a **warning**: *anyone who can reach this controller reads its fleet without signing in: pools, hosts, runners, jobs, usage and runner logs. Writes, people and settings stay behind sign-in.* The fix is *turn security.public_view off unless this controller is meant to be public*. With `security.disable_auth` on as well the finding is not raised: every request is already an administrator, and `auth.disabled` says so. ### 2. The visitor `auth.Authenticate` resolves a request with no credential at all to a visitor when the setting is on, instead of `ErrNoCredentials`: - `Kind` is a new `KindPublic` (`"public"`), `ID` `"public"`, `Name` `"public visitor"`, `Role` viewer. - `Scopes` is a fixed list, `auth.VisitorScopes`. The role alone is too wide: a viewer reads the audit log (usernames and client addresses), their own tokens and assistant conversations, and the AI context's source files. A visitor carries exactly these, each a read: `pools:read`, `runners:read`, `jobs:read`, `usage:read`, `hosts:read`, `providers:read`, `machines:read`, `installations:read`, `webhooks:read`, `updates:read`, `kennel:read`, `events:read`, `logs:read`, `stats:read`. `Allowed` already treats scopes as a ceiling below the role, so every route's existing `require` refuses the rest with no new check. A test holds the list to the rule that every entry is a viewer's action and a read. What stays strict: - **A bearer token that does not check out is still 401.** Automation with a revoked token must hear that, not quietly become a visitor. - **A session cookie that does not check out falls back to a visitor**, and the response clears the cookie. A visitor whose session lapsed is a visitor; a 401 there would strand them on a sign-in form with a cookie they cannot remove, since sign-out is itself behind authentication. - **A credential the controller could not check** (`ErrAuthBackend`) is a 500 as today, never a visitor. `auth.Explain` words a visitor's refusal for them: *this is a read-only public view; sign in to do this*. Nothing else in the 403 changes. ### 3. The account routes The `/auth/*` routes behind authentication carry no action, because each is the caller's own: sign out, preferences, password, two-step, MCP consent and connections. A visitor has none of those, and signing out writes an audit row, so an anonymous loop could fill the audit log. A middleware on that group lets a visitor reach `GET /auth/session` and nothing else; every other route answers 403 with the visitor's sentence. ### 4. The event stream The stream sends every frame to anyone holding `events.read` and narrows a few kinds by role. That was already too wide for a token scoped to `events:read` alone, which received audit rows, and it is far too wide for a visitor. Each frame is now sent only to a caller who could read it with `GET`: a table maps every bus kind to the read action that covers it (`runner.*` to `runners.read`, `audit` to `audit.read`, `problems.updated` and `stats` to `stats.read`, and so on), resolved per frame like the existing filters. A kind missing from the table is dropped, and a test walks every kind the bus defines so a new one cannot ship unmapped. ### 5. MCP `/mcp` authenticates through `auth.Authenticate`, so with the setting on an anonymous MCP client is a visitor. The tools that change the fleet are already offered only to a caller `auth.Allowed` lets use them, so a visitor is offered none. The read tools are offered to everyone by design, and the API refuses what a credential cannot read: a visitor calling an AI context tool is told the public view does not show it. A person who wants more connects with an API token in the `Authorization` header; MCP OAuth is not offered to an anonymous client on a public view, because an unauthenticated request is answered rather than challenged. ### 6. The UI - `GET /meta` carries `public_view`. - The session store learns `visitor` (an identity of kind `public`). Its `can` answers false for every role above viewer, as a viewer's does. - A visitor sees a slim line under the top bar: *You are looking at a public, read-only view of this fleet.* with a **Sign in** link, which opens the sign-in form; the form gains **Continue without signing in** when `public_view` is on. - The user menu says *Visitor* and offers **Sign in** in place of sign-out. - Audit, Settings, Eli repairs and Migrate are left out of the navigation, the command palette and the `g` shortcuts for a visitor, and the Eli widget is not shown: each would only answer 403. ### 7. The landing page The button keeps pointing at the local demo until `demo.zoomies.sh` answers, because a button that leads nowhere is worse than one that asks for a terminal. Once the instance is up, the runbook's last step changes `docs/index.md` so **Try the demo** opens `https://demo.zoomies.sh` and the local command moves below it as *or run the demo on your own machine*. ## The demo deployment (runbook, the owner's) `docs/instapods.md` is the general guide to running Zoomies on InstaPods, and `deploy/instapods/` holds the build and start scripts both pods run. The demo is that guide with these choices: ```mermaid flowchart LR gh["GitHub: the zoomies-demo organisation"] -->|webhooks| web["web pod: zoomies controller,
public view on"] worker["worker pod: zoomies agent,
process backend"] -->|"long-polls, outbound only"| web worker -->|"registers runners, runs jobs"| gh visitors["visitors and their assistants"] -->|"https, no sign-in"| web ``` 1. **Organisation.** Create `zoomies-demo` on GitHub with three or four public repositories, each with a workflow on `schedule` (every ten minutes, offset per repository) and `workflow_dispatch` only: a short build, a matrix of a few jobs, one longer job, and one that fails on purpose now and then so the failure views have something in them. **No secrets**: a visitor reads every log. Set the organisation's Actions policy to require approval for every outside contributor, because the runners are processes in a pod rather than throwaway containers. `runs-on` names the demo pool's labels. The workflows, a keep-alive and the organisation's settings are in `deploy/demo-org/`. 2. **Keep the schedules alive.** GitHub disables a scheduled workflow after sixty days without repository activity. A monthly workflow in one repository commits a timestamp to each, or the owner re-enables them from the API. 3. **The web pod.** A Go-preset pod on the Build plan, connected to `github.com/eyupio/zoomies` with auto-deploy off, using the guide's install, build and start commands for the controller. Set `ZOOMIES_EXTERNAL_URL` to the pod's address (or `https://demo.zoomies.sh` once the custom domain is attached), `ZOOMIES_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, `ZOOMIES_VERSION=dev` and `ZOOMIES_PUBLIC_VIEW=true`. Create the first account, connect the GitHub App for the organisation, and create one pool for the process backend. 4. **The worker pod.** A second Go-preset pod, converted to a worker so it has no public address, using the guide's commands for the agent, with `ZOOMIES_CONTROLLER_URL` and a join token from **Hosts, Add a host**. Size it for the jobs: Grow (2 vCPU, 4 GB) runs two at a time comfortably. 5. **Name and limits.** Attach `demo.zoomies.sh` to the web pod. Each visitor holds an event stream open, under `limits.visitor_event_subscribers` (200 by default), a ceiling of their own that never takes the streams the people running the demo need; raise it to what the plan carries and watch it. 6. **Check it.** The problems list carries `auth.public_view` and nothing worse; a private window lands on the Overview with the read-only line; an assistant pointed at `/mcp` with no credential lists pools. 7. **Flip the button.** Change **Try the demo** in `docs/index.md` as section 7 says. ## Tests - `internal/auth`: an anonymous caller is a visitor with the setting on and is refused with it off; a bad bearer token is 401 either way; a lapsed session is a visitor with it on and 401 with it off; every visitor scope is a viewer's read; a visitor is refused the audit log, tokens and assistant actions; the visitor's refusal sentence. - `internal/config`: `auth.public_view` is a warning when the setting is on and absent with `security.disable_auth`; the settings registry row. - `internal/api`: a visitor reads every route its scopes name and is refused every write; the account routes refuse a visitor but `GET /auth/session`; a visitor signing out writes no audit row; the lapsed cookie is cleared; `/meta` says `public_view`; a stream sends an audit frame only to a caller who may read the audit log; every bus kind has a read action. - `web/unit`: the navigation a visitor sees. ## Docs and generated files `docs/public-view.md` (what it is for, what a visitor sees and cannot, MCP), `docs/security.md`, `docs/configuration.md`, `docs/problem-codes.md` and the catalogue it generates, `docs/api-surface.md`, `docs/mcp.md`, `api/openapi.yaml` with `openapi_spec.go` and `schema.d.ts` regenerated, and `mkdocs.yml`. ## Risks and how each is bounded - **A scope list that drifts from the role table.** Bounded by the test that every visitor scope is a viewer's read, and by `Allowed` refusing anything not listed: a new read action is hidden from visitors until somebody adds it. - **A route with no action that writes.** The account group is the only such group behind authentication; it is closed to visitors as a whole. - **Load from strangers.** Visitors' event streams have a ceiling of their own, `limits.visitor_event_subscribers`, and are not counted against `limits.event_subscribers`, so a crowd cannot lock out the people running the demo; the runbook puts a rate limit in front as well. Watching a running job's log asks the agent for a stream, so the demo pool stays small. - **A demo workflow that prints a secret.** The organisation holds none. - **Jobs that are processes, not containers.** Pods offer no Docker, so a job runs as the worker pod's user and a later job can see what an earlier one left outside its work directory. Bounded by running only the organisation's own scheduled workflows, requiring approval for outside contributors, and keeping the worker pod free of anything but the agent's own token. ## Not included - An animated fixture fleet. The live fleet is the demo; the local demo stays a still life. - Eli in the public view, and any model spend on visitors. - A per-address rate limit inside the controller. It belongs in front of it.

# ZF-240: the fleet as it moves, over MCP Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** An agent over MCP, and Eli, can read what the fleet did in the last few minutes and wait, bounded, for the next change, without the transport holding a session.

**Architecture:** One new route, `GET /events/recent`, reads the event bus's ring as JSON and can hold a request for at most 25 seconds until something matching arrives; the stream's replay and this route share one function on the bus so they cannot disagree about what was lost. Ten MCP tools are each one call to a documented route through the `API` interface; the two that read the ring render each frame as a line of trusted fields and quote workflow-written names in the untrusted block the log tool already uses. Eli is offered seven of them; a `live` flag on a tool stops Eli answering a repeated wait from its result cache.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27 standard library; `internal/events`, `internal/api`, `internal/mcp`, `internal/controller`; the Svelte starters file for one new opening question; `api/openapi.yaml` and its two generated clients.

**Spec:** `roadmap/fleet-analysis.md` section 4 (and sections 2, 6, 7 and 9). This plan amends it once: `list_workflow_runs`, `scaling_decisions`, `fleet_samples`, `host_samples` and `runner_timeline` answer the route's JSON as `list_jobs` does, and only the two ring tools render lines with an untrusted block, because every other list tool already hands a model names inline and a second convention would be the odd one.

## Global Constraints

- `make build-nogui` first on a fresh checkout; before every push `make fmt`, `make lint`, `make test`, `go mod tidy` leaves `go.mod`/`go.sum` unchanged.
- After editing `api/openapi.yaml`: `go run internal/api/gen_openapi.go` from the repository root and `make openapi`, and commit both outputs. After adding a tool or a command: `make generate` (it rewrites `skills/zoomies/reference.md` and `skills/zoomies/mcp-reference.md`) and commit them.
- British spelling in prose; comments say why; no em dash anywhere (`internal/docs/no_em_dash_test.go`); imperative plain-prose commit messages with no prefix; every new behaviour arrives with a test seen to fail first.
- Commits end with the two attribution lines from the session reminder; no model identifier in anything pushed.
- The MCP transport stays stateless: no session id, no server-initiated stream, `resources.subscribe` stays false.
- A tool is one request to one documented route with the caller's own credential; `internal/mcp` imports neither the store nor the bus.
- Every window is capped: at most 200 rows and `maxWindowBlock = 64 << 10` bytes of rendered text, truncated with the id to continue from.
- A wait is at most 25 seconds (`maxWait = 25 * time.Second`), so one call sits inside Eli's 30-second tool timeout.

## Review Focus

1. A client that passes a `since` from another run of the process must be told `complete: false`, never handed an empty window that reads as "nothing happened". Pinned in Task 2 by `TestRecentEventsFromAnotherEpochIsIncomplete`.
2. A `wait` while the ring already holds matching events past `since` must return at once with them, or a model spends its one call waiting for a change that already happened. Pinned in Task 2 by `TestWaitForChangeAnswersAtOnceWhenEventsAlreadyExist`.
3. A frame whose payload carries a job name with an instruction in it must reach the model only inside the untrusted block. Pinned in Task 4 by `TestAWindowRendersAJobNameOnlyInTheUntrustedBlock`.
4. A wait must count against `limits.event_subscribers` and release its subscription on every exit, or a model's waits exhaust the browser's streams. Pinned in Task 2 by `TestWaitIsCappedAndCountsAsAStream`.
5. A viewer's Eli asked for the audit log must be told the tool is not one it was offered, not handed the route's 403 text. Pinned in Task 6 by the allowlist test and `TestEliRefusesAnAdminReadByName`.

### Task 2: `GET /events/recent`, with a bounded wait

**Files:**
- Create: `internal/api/handlers_events.go`, `internal/api/handlers_events_test.go`
- Modify: `internal/api/router.go:201` (register beside `/events`), `api/openapi.yaml` (beside `/events`), `internal/api/openapi_spec.go` and `web/src/lib/api/schema.d.ts` (regenerated), `docs/api-surface.md` (Overview section, one row)

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `Bus.Recent`, `Bus.SubscribeWithin`, `Bus.ParseWireID`, `Bus.WireID`, `parseKinds` and `lastEventID` from `sse.go`, `queryDuration`, `queryInt`, `clamp`, `writeJSON`, `badRequestField`, `limitReached`, `s.cfg().Limits.EventSubscribers`.
- Produces: route `GET /api/v1/events/recent`, action `auth.ActionEventsRead` (viewer). Query: `since` (a wire id as the stream sends it, or a duration such as `10m`; absent means the whole ring), `kinds` (comma-separated), `topic` (prefix), `limit` (default 50, maximum 200), `wait` (a duration, 0 by default, capped to `maxWait`). Body:

```json
{"items":[{"id":"<epoch>.<seq>","kind":"job.updated","topic":"job:job_x","at":"...","data":{...}}],
 "next":"<epoch>.<seq>","complete":true,"truncated":false,"timed_out":false}
```

`next` is the last item's id, or the ring's newest id when nothing matched (so a first call establishes a cursor). A `since` duration selects events with `At` at or after now minus the duration. With `wait > 0` and no matching items, the handler subscribes with `SubscribeWithin(ctx, opts{Replay: since}, limit)` (a refusal is the stream's 409), returns the first matching event plus whatever is already queued behind it without blocking, or `timed_out: true` with empty items at the deadline. A `since` from another epoch sets `complete: false` and reads from the ring's start.

# Bounding the generated `zoomies-ai-context` branch

**Status**: proposed, drafted on 16 October 2026 at the owner's request ("bound its
history"). Nothing here has been run. The one-time step rewrites a published
branch, so it is the owner's to run.

## The problem

The managed workflow (`zoomies-ai-context.yml`, template 1) publishes a new commit
to `zoomies-ai-context` after every push to `main`, with the previous tip as its
parent. Each commit carries `.zoomies/ai-context/snapshot.json`, which is about
26.9 MB at the tip (the limit is 32 MiB), and a manifest.

| Measured on 16 October, in a clone of this repository | |
| --- | --- |
| Commits on the branch | 353, one chain with one root, from 3 to 16 October |
| Blobs on it | 707, about 373 MiB on disk once delta-compressed |
| Whole pack of a full clone | 261.5 MiB |
| Growth | about 1 MiB per push to `main`; at the pace so far (27 pushes a day) about 29 MiB a day |

Everyone who clones without `--single-branch` downloads all of it, and every
fresh CI checkout does too unless it fetches one branch.

## What constrains the fix

These are read from the code and the docs, not assumed.

* **The product promises no force push.** `docs/ai-context.md` says publication
  "moves the `zoomies-ai-context` branch forward without a force push", and
  `internal/aicontext/README.md` says it "moves only the owned generated branch
  without force". The workflow does a fast-forward from the exact parent it read,
  so that "a competing publication fails rather than replacing a newer snapshot".
* **The workflow checks the tip before it publishes.** The tip must carry
  `.zoomies/ai-context/NOTICE.md` with the expected text, a commit message that
  starts `Publish Zoomies AI Context` followed by a newline, and a tree of exactly
  the files the template writes. Anything else is refused as "no recognised
  ownership". A rewritten branch has to pass those three checks.
* **Readers use the tip, not the history.** The documented local route is
  `git fetch origin zoomies-ai-context` and `git show` of the manifest and snapshot
  from the same commit; Zoomies' own retrieval pages carry the source commit
  recorded inside the manifest. Nothing reads an earlier generated commit.
  Removing history loses nothing a reader uses, and a reader that pinned an
  older generated SHA keeps working only while GitHub still holds the object.
* **A destination that writes no branch already exists.** The workflow's
  `destination` is `both` here. *Zoomies only* uploads the snapshot over OIDC and
  creates no branch at all.

## Options

### A. Stop writing the branch for this repository (smallest change)

Choose *Zoomies only* through the product's own Amend pull request. The branch
stops growing today. The cost is the branch route for this repository: an
assistant with no Zoomies connection can no longer `git fetch` the context, which
`.zoomies/AI_CONTEXT.md` describes as an available route. Nothing about the
product changes.

### B. Keep `both`, and squash the branch on a schedule (this repository only)

A daily workflow in this repository replaces the branch with one commit holding
the current tip's tree, using the same message the managed workflow writes, so the
ownership checks above still pass and the next publication fast-forwards from it.
The branch is forced, which the product itself never does, so the workflow is
ours and not part of the managed template. Growth is bounded to about a day of
pushes (some 30 MiB). It needs a token that may force-push that one ref.

### C. Change the template so the branch is always one commit (every installation)

Template 2 publishes a parentless commit and updates the ref with `force: true`
after checking the ref still equals the tip it read (the REST API has no
compare-and-swap, so a very short race window remains; the concurrency group
already serialises runs). This fixes the weight for every repository that uses
Zoomies AI Context, and is also the only option that reverses a documented
guarantee. It needs `template_version` 2, template 1 kept as a recognised older
generation (`olderGenerations` in `internal/aicontext/workflow.go`), the ownership
check reading the tip rather than a parent chain, updates to `docs/ai-context.md`
and the README, tests for both generations, and a repair pull request for every
installation to adopt it.

**Recommendation:** A now, and the one-time squash below, because together they
stop the growth and remove the weight without touching the product. Do C only if
the branch route matters enough to keep, since B is a workaround for the same
thing in one repository.

## The one-time squash

Run from a clone whose `origin` is `eyupio/zoomies`. It keeps a local bundle of
the old tip first, which is the rollback.

```sh
git fetch origin zoomies-ai-context:refs/remotes/origin/zoomies-ai-context
old=$(git rev-parse refs/remotes/origin/zoomies-ai-context)
git bundle create "$HOME/zoomies-ai-context-before-squash.bundle" refs/remotes/origin/zoomies-ai-context

src=$(git log -1 --format=%B "$old" | sed -n 's/^Source: //p')
new=$(printf 'Publish Zoomies AI Context\n\nSource: %s\n' "$src" | git commit-tree "$old^{tree}")

# --force-with-lease fails if the branch moved since the fetch above.
git push --force-with-lease=refs/heads/zoomies-ai-context:"$old" \
  origin "$new:refs/heads/zoomies-ai-context"
```

Do it between pushes to `main`, or while the workflow is idle, so a publication is
not in flight. If a ruleset blocks force pushes to that branch, lift it for the
push and put it back.

### Check it worked

1. A fresh `git clone https://github.com/eyupio/zoomies.git` is a fraction of
   261 MiB, and `git rev-list --count origin/zoomies-ai-context` is 1.
2. `git show origin/zoomies-ai-context:.zoomies/ai-context/NOTICE.md` still
   reads as before, and the commit message begins `Publish Zoomies AI Context`.
3. The next push to `main` runs the workflow to success, and the branch has two
   commits. A refusal here ("no recognised ownership") means the squash did not
   keep the message or the tree; restore the old tip and look again.
4. The repository page in Zoomies still shows the context as verified.

### Roll back

```sh
git fetch "$HOME/zoomies-ai-context-before-squash.bundle" \
  refs/remotes/origin/zoomies-ai-context:refs/heads/restore-ai-context
git push --force origin restore-ai-context:refs/heads/zoomies-ai-context
```

The squashed-away commits stay fetchable by SHA on GitHub for a while after they
become unreachable, but not for ever, so the bundle is the rollback that lasts.

## Decisions for the owner

1. Which of A, B or C. A is recommended above.
2. Whether to run the squash now. It is safe to defer, but the branch gains
   about 1 MiB with every push in the meantime.

# Eli automatic repairs: visibility and controls Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Let an administrator see which repositories repair themselves, what that has cost and done, and stop it, on the hub, the attempt page and the repair page.

**Architecture:** Two additive administrator routes over existing tables (an overview of Automatic policies with their allowance, health and latest repair, and a stop that only relaxes a policy), and readiness naming the repository's mode. The UI adds a hub panel and a stop dialog, a card on an automatic repair's page and a note on the repair page, over a pure, unit-tested helper module.

**Tech Stack:** Go 1.27 (store, controller, API), SQLite through `internal/store` only, Svelte 5 runes, TypeScript, Vite, Playwright, OpenAPI 3.1 with generated Go and TypeScript copies.

**Spec:** [2026-10-18-eli-automatic-repairs.md](2026-10-18-eli-automatic-repairs.md)

> **Where the build departed from this plan.** The store's activity read takes the
> repositories it answers for, so its scan for the newest row can stop early and
> no index is needed. There is no "installation removed" problem, because a
> policy is deleted with its installation, and a deleted provider leaves the
> policy with none. The controller keeps a failed save as that repository's result
> and carries on with the rest. The repair page's note takes the repository's row
> of the overview, which can say whose allowance stopped an automatic repair and
> carries a provider problem as the better reason, in place of a spent-allowance
> flag. The client does not sort the rows again, because the controller orders
> them. The stop (send, toast, stay open with the reason) lives once in
> `lib/repairs/stop.ts`. The note reads only for an administrator, only on a
> repository that is automatic and only while the failure has not been fixed,
> closed or replaced. The audits found two overflows, in the shared breadcrumb and
> in the new card, both fixed with `overflow-wrap`. The screenshot fixture seeds two
> automatic repositories, so the hub and setup images were retaken and an attempt
> image was added.

## Global Constraints

* Go 1.27.1 or later; Node 22 or later. No new dependency, Go or npm (`docs/dependencies.md`).
* SQL is written in `internal/store` only. No migration.
* After editing `api/openapi.yaml` run `make openapi` and commit both generated files (`internal/api/openapi_spec.go`, `web/src/lib/api/schema.d.ts`). A new route also updates the route and role table in `internal/api/api_test.go` and `docs/api-surface.md` in the same task.
* Prose, comments, docs, error messages and UI strings: British spelling; no em dashes; no spaced `--`; an absent value is `NO_VALUE` from `web/src/lib/format.ts`.
* UI: tokens only, never a raw colour or a value that already has a token; the six status hues keep their fixed meanings and every status comes from `web/src/lib/status.ts`; no state-management library, charting library or router change; the app shell stays under 200 KB gzipped, so every new component lives in an existing lazily loaded route.
* Nothing is reachable from the UI that is not on a documented REST route.
* A new component state is added to the gallery (`web/src/gallery/`) before a route reaches it.
* A repository that is not automatic adds nothing to any page. Stopping never turns anything on.
* Everything a workflow, a person or an operator names (repository, provider and model names) is untrusted: rendered as text, and a link only when its scheme is `http` or `https`.
* Tests: standard-library `testing`, table-driven, `:memory:` stores, injected clocks, the fake GitHub; test names are sentences about behaviour. UI unit fixtures are built to the generated types, never cast.
* Commit messages: an imperative sentence in plain prose, sentence case, no prefix. Each commit ends with the two attribution lines the session was given.

## Review Focus

* A policy whose provider was deleted still stops, because that is the day the control is needed. Owned by Task 3.
* An ordinary user is refused the overview and sees one sentence on the repair page, never what Eli has done. Owned by Task 4 and Task 8.
* A lowered daily limit leaves a repository with more attempts used than allowed; the row reads "all used", never a negative or a bar past full. Owned by Task 5.
* A repository, provider or model name holding markup renders as text and never overflows a phone. Owned by Task 9.
* Stopping a repository somebody else already stopped is a neutral "already stopped", not an error. Owned by Task 3 and Task 6.
* The last repository stopping removes the panel without leaving keyboard focus on nothing. Owned by Task 6.
* A repair that is queued when its repository is stopped does not run. Owned by Task 3.
